items.title: L-6: uninstalling the Cloudflare app is what clears the check
items.body:
## Summary
- Completes **L-6**. The last step was not the one the plan named: deleting the Worker (PR #14) left the Workers Builds project alive and unreachable, because that project is not part of the Worker and Cloudflare's UI reaches Builds from inside a Worker's Settings. The dashboard answer to `boy-concept` was "Failed to find Worker", which is the orphan, not a typo.
- The check run is created by the GitHub App `cloudflare-workers-and-pages` (id 85455), which is also what receives the push. Ademola uninstalled that app, so both the trigger and the reporter are gone, whatever record still sits in Cloudflare's CI store.
- The repo carries no webhook, and neither credential can reach the pipeline from a terminal: the spike token gets 12006 on `/builds/*` (it has Workers Scripts, not Workers Builds) and the GitHub PAT gets 403 on `/user/installations`. Both now recorded in the spike doc.
- Cost named for later: any Phase 1 build pipeline starts by reinstalling that app, with its deploy command set to `npm run deploy:test`. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (new D30 text + section 10, README deploy note, spike doc account state and Open row, ROADMAP risk bullet, row and log line).

## Test plan

items.title: L-6: the stub Worker is deleted; the orphaned Builds project still fails CI
items.body:
## Summary
Half a fix, and this PR is the evidence for that. L-6 goes to `[~]`, not `[x]`.

- **Diagnosis** (Certain, from API reads): the red check is not GitHub Actions, `roadmap-and-structure` passes. It comes from the GitHub App `cloudflare-workers-and-pages` (id 85455) running a Workers Builds project keyed to a Cloudflare Worker service named `boy-concept`: the onboarding hello-world stub, created `2026-10-27T08:12:44Z`, never modified, never reachable (`boy-concept.ademola2993k.workers.dev` answers 404 / Cloudflare error 1042), and never this repo's target, whose only wrangler config is `worker/wrangler.toml` (`name = "boy-concept-spike"`). It ran `npx wrangler deploy` from a workspace root with no `wrangler.toml`, so it could not pass.
- **Chosen fix** (Ademola, from four options): delete the stub rather than rewire the command. Rewiring to `npm run deploy:test` was rejected because that command deploys the spike rig, so every push would publish something nobody asked for and deploy authority would sit outside the repo.
- **Done**: `DELETE /accounts/{account_id}/workers/scripts/boy-concept` succeeded. The account now holds one service, `boy-concept-spike`, and `boy-concept` answers error 10007.
- **What this PR falsified**: the head commit picked up a *new* failing build, `957afefc-ccb7-41a6-a014-aee28bf51361`. A Workers Builds project is a separate object that outlives its Worker, so this one now sits orphaned, its dashboard link still reading `/workers/services/view/boy-concept/production`, and it still posts the check.
- **Left**: deleting that project in the Cloudflare dashboard. No credential in reach can do it: the spike token gets 12006 "Invalid token" on `/builds/workers/{tag}/triggers` (no Workers Builds scope) and this PAT gets 403 on `/user/installations`.
- **Docs**: `D30` + section 10 in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (v0.12), the README deploy note states one pipeline plus the expected red check, the spike doc's account state and Open table carry the corrected state, and `ROADMAP.md` has the risk bullet, the `[~]` row and a log line. Scorecard unchanged: Must 20 of 86, Should 1 of 8.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run lint` clean, `npm run typecheck` green, `npm test` 29 passed
- [x] Cloudflare read-back after the delete, above
- [x] `roadmap-and-structure` passes on both commits
- [ ] **Expected failure**: `Workers Builds: boy-concept` fails on this PR too. That is the finding, not a regression, and it is what keeps L-6 open.
- [ ] After the dashboard deletes the project, the next push should show only `roadmap-and-structure`; that check closes L-6 and moves Should to 2 of 8.

items.title: P-5: projects collection, verified and publish_ok, the build guard
items.body:
## Task IDs

P-5. Also touches P-6 and P-8 (both now unblocked, with a note each), D28, ESSENTIALS rules 8 and 16.

## What changed

The content layer now exists. `web/src/content-rules.ts` holds the projects schema, the bracket scan that backs the verification guard (`bracketedFieldsIn`) and the two render predicates (`shorableProjects`, `placeholderProjects`). It is pure and imports no Astro virtual module, which is why the guard can be unit-tested without a build. `web/src/content.config.ts` is only the wiring: a glob loader over `web/src/content/projects/*.yaml`, so Astro validates every entry at sync and build, and a violation fails the build. The entry id is the file name stem, which is the slug P-7 routes on; there is no `slug` field, so a file cannot disagree with its own name.

`demo: true` (D28) is the decision that makes the placeholder rule safe. The grid falls back to entries *explicitly marked* as placeholders, never to "everything unverified", so real work with no permission yet (a private wedding) renders in neither mode. The schema refuses `demo: true` beside `verified: true` or `publish_ok: true`. Chosen over component-held DEMO cards and a `demo-` filename convention.

Four demo entries, one per category, with every unknown bracketed, so C-2 replaces files rather than rewriting code. `PortfolioGrid.astro` reads the collection and maps its chips over the same `projectCategories` list the schema accepts, which removes the duplicated category list. `ProjectCard.astro` keeps the labelled poster frame until P-6 resolves a real poster path.

Also corrected: ARCHITECTURE section 11 claimed CI runs lint, typecheck, tests and the build on every PR. It does not; `ci.yml` is the two doc-discipline checks. Section 11 now says what is true, and records that the guard therefore bites at build and deploy, not at PR review.

- [x] `content/PLACEHOLDERS.md` and `content/copy.md`: the per-project bracket row now points at the four files, and the categories line records that `projectCategories` is the source

## Checks

- [x] No invented content. Fixture values (`Fixture Client`, `https://example.invalid/fixture`) exist only inside the test file; every value in the four content files is bracketed and registered

  - `npm run lint`: clean. `npm run typecheck`: `astro check` 18 files, 0 errors; worker `tsc` clean. `npm test`: 18 passed (15 new). `npm run build`: 2 pages

items.title: P-25: responsive and design-system conformance pass

## Summary
- Audited the built page with Anthropic's official `frontend-design` skill, measuring through iframes at 320, 375, 390, 768, 1024, 1200 and 1440 px. Four DESIGN rules were being broken and all four are now met and re-measured.
- **Breakpoints.** The build ran on Tailwind's 640 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 scale instead of DESIGN section 5's 768 / 1200 / 1440, which is why a 1024 px screen showed three portfolio posters and five 176 px process columns with 128 px of usable text. `--breakpoint-*` is reset and re-declared as md 768, lg 1200, xl 1440, so an unlisted variant emits no CSS, and `design-tokens.test.ts` now fails on `sm:`, `xs:` or `2xl:` in `web/src`. The built stylesheet emits only 768, 1200 and 1440 queries.
- **Tap targets.** Section 5 asks for at least 44 x 44 px and nothing met it: filter chips were 32 px and the desktop nav links 17 px. Chips that are controls are 44 px, label chips inside cards stay 32 px, and the nav links and brand got a 44 px target with no visual change.
- **Gutters.** The 40 px desktop step existed in the design and in zero components. One `.container-site` (`px-5 md:px-8 lg:px-10`) replaces ten private copies.
- **Structure.** Process is now a numbered rail (five columns can never exceed 211 px inside a 1200 px container, so the old grid was wrong at every width) with the heading beside it from 1200 px. The decorative Q1 to Q4 markers and the 1 to 13 field numbers are gone, and the nav prints "Work", the word the section already used.

## What this does

Answers ARCHITECTURE Verify item 5 with the spike Worker as the test rig, and adds the first real file of the header plan: `web/public/_headers` with the CSP from section 8 plus nosniff, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Permissions-Policy and HSTS.

## Result

| Probe | _headers applied |
|---|---|
| `GET /` (asset) | yes, all six headers |
| `GET /index.html` (307 from assets) | yes, on the redirect too |
| `GET /api/ping`, `POST /api/spike` | no, not one header |
| `GET /missing.html`, `GET /projects/x` (asset miss falling through to the Worker) | no |

So `_headers` governs the asset layer only. Three consequences, recorded as decision D21:

1. B-11 keeps `_headers` for pages, and the site does **not** need `run_worker_first = true` just to make headers apply everywhere, which would have put every asset request through the Worker.
2. The Worker must set its own security headers in Hono middleware for `/api/*`. B-11's task text now says so.
3. Once `not_found_handling` and `404.astro` exist, B-11 re-tests what a 404 response carries, because today a miss becomes an unprotected Worker response (D19).

Local parity holds: `wrangler dev` applies the same block, so a header mistake surfaces in dev rather than only at the edge.

The CSP is applied, but its values are dead letters until the real scripts exist: Turnstile, GA4 and the YouTube nocookie frame are only exercised at P-4 and P-12. `style-src 'unsafe-inline'` is provisional and should be tightened if Tailwind v4 emits a single stylesheet. items.title: Fix issues: 235
items.body:
This PR resolves the following assigned issues:

- closes #235
- closes #231 
- closes #242 

## Why this is a coverage PR, not a component PR

Issue #235 asks to *"Create a reusable ErrorBoundary component **or page-level error boundaries**"* with a *"Try again" reset trigger* and *clean error logging*. At `main` = `e34ebf19`, the reusable component **already exists and already meets all three acceptance criteria**, so I deliberately did **not** rewrite `src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx` — doing so would be inventing work. It already ships:

- `resetKey?: string | number` with reset-on-prop-change (`:12`, `:55-57`)
- a private `retry` and a design-token fallback card with a **Try again** button (`:61`, `:89-90`)
- message-only logging in production (`console.error(`${prefix} ${error.message}`)`, `:48`) versus the full-stack dev branch (`:50`), so no sensitive runtime data is exposed in prod.

What was missing was **mount coverage**. Before this PR, `grep -rn ErrorBoundary src` showed wraps in exactly one route — `src/app/(dashboard)/agents/page.tsx` (import `:7`, wraps `:44`, `:47`, `:50`, `:77`) — i.e. "agent monitors" from #235's list were done, but **wallets** and **policies** had zero boundaries. This PR closes exactly that gap, in the style `agents/page.tsx` uses: one `<ErrorBoundary section="…">` per independently failing widget section, not one wrapper around the whole page.

## Changes made

`src/app/(dashboard)/wallets/page.tsx` (two widget sections, previously 0 boundaries):
- `<ErrorBoundary section="Wallet summary">` around the Total value / Wallets / Active stat-card grid (`:54`)
- `<ErrorBoundary section="Wallet list">` around the wallet-cards grid (`:74`)

`src/app/(dashboard)/policies/[id]/page.tsx` (four widget sections, previously 0 boundaries):
- `<ErrorBoundary section="Policy details">` around the key/value detail card (`:77`)
- `<ErrorBoundary section="Policy configuration" resetKey={data.id}>` around the Configuration card — the one place with a naturally changing key (`:105`)
- `<ErrorBoundary section="Policy simulator">` around the dry-run simulator card incl. `SimulationResult` (`:123`)
- `<ErrorBoundary section="Transaction simulator">` around `<TransactionSimulator />` (`:163`)

Nothing else changed: no edits to the boundary component, no new dependencies, no other files.

## Verification — the repo has no test runner

`package.json` has only `dev/build/start/lint/typecheck/format`; there are zero `*.test.*`/`*.spec.*` files and no jest/vitest/playwright config. **No tests were added and no "tests pass" claim is made.** The gates were run on pristine `main` first, then on this branch (all inside a 3200 MB memory-bounded systemd scope):

| Gate | baseline `main` (`e34ebf1`) | this branch (`61f14e6`) |
|---|---|---|
| `npm run typecheck` | exit 0, 0 TS errors | exit 0, 0 TS errors |
| `npm run build` | exit 0 | exit 0; route manifest includes `/wallets` (4.45 kB) and `/policies/[id]` (7.45 kB) |
| `npm run lint` | exit 0, "No ESLint warnings or errors" | exit 0, "No ESLint warnings or errors" |

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs build/typecheck/lint on **Node 20**; local execution here measured `node -v` = **v22.22.1**, so local runs are not byte-identical to CI and I do not imply they are.

## Fallback + "Try again" actually render (manual proof, per the issue's "trigger an intentional render error" ask)

Started `npm run dev` (mock mode; `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` empty ⇒ `isMockMode`) and, since these are client-rendered widget trees, verified the **post-hydration DOM with headless Chrome**:

- `GET /wallets` → **200**; hydrated DOM contains the wrapped widgets normally (`Total value` ×1) with **0** fallback strings.
- `GET /policies/pol_max_txn` → **200** (real mock id from `src/services/mock/entities.ts`); hydrated DOM contains `Dry-run a spend against every active policy` ×1, `Run simulation` ×1, **0** fallback strings. Not a 500 anywhere.

Then a **temporary, never-committed** synthetic throw: a `L130Probe` child component (rendered *inside* the boundary's subtree, not in the parent's render frame) throwing `Error('L130-synthetic-render-error-probe')` inside `<ErrorBoundary section="Wallet list">`. The boundary caught it — asserted strings, each count-checked against the served DOM:

- `This section failed to render` ×1 — exact h3 text of `ErrorBoundary.tsx:81`; the route did **not** fall through to `(dashboard)/error.tsx` (`Something went wrong` ×0), which is the "one failing widget no longer crashes the page" behavior.
- `Try again` ×1 with the `lucide-refresh-cw` icon — the reset trigger at `:89-90`.
- Dev fallback paragraph rendered the raw message (`:86` dev branch), and the **browser console** (captured via `--enable-logging=stderr`) showed the `[ErrorBoundary: Wallet list] caught a component error:` prefix — i.e. the **`componentStack` branch at `:50` fired, not the message-only `:48` branch**, because `next dev` runs with `NODE_ENV=development`; the message-only prod branch at `:48` is the path taken in production builds and is what satisfies AC line 3 there.
- The sibling `Wallet summary` boundary kept rendering (`Total value` ×1) while `Wallet list` was in its fallback — independent-failure isolation, demonstrated.

The probe was then reverted (`git checkout -- 'src/app/(dashboard)/wallets/page.tsx'`); `git status` shows a clean tree with only the two committed route files in the diff, and the post-revert hydrated DOM again renders `Total value` with 0 fallback strings. The scaffolding was never committed.

## Non-collision statement (measured contention)

- `src/app/(dashboard)/policies/page.tsx` was **avoided** — external PR **#311** (`EddyGiggs77`) is actively rewriting that file.
- `src/app/(dashboard)/wallets/[id]/page.tsx` was **avoided** — five open PRs touch it: **#440** (Uhiara), **#435** (lightnoor890), **#323** (kali-el), **#322** (ciscokwiz), **#254** (Ayomikun2005).

items.title: fix(db): sum settled /stats amounts in SQL on Postgres (#60)
items.body:
Part of #60 — the follow-up to merged #120. **Please do not treat this as closing #60**: AC 1 (schema columns as `Decimal`/numeric) needs a maintainer decision this PR cannot make, explained below and in `docs/amount-numeric-migration-plan.md`.

## What #60 needs, and where each AC stands after this PR

- **AC 2 — migration plan documented: already delivered by #120** (`prisma/postgres-pending/20260107000000_amount_numeric_to_decimal/migration.sql` + the plan doc). Not re-delivered here.
- **AC 3 — sums done in SQL; route tests unchanged: delivered for the deploy database (Postgres) by this PR.** Not every route test scenario runs on Postgres yet (that is open issue #14), so on SQLite the exact JavaScript pass intentionally stays — see "Why the SQLite branch remains".
- **AC 1 — amount columns stored as `Decimal`/numeric in the committed schema: NOT attempted, needs a maintainer decision.** Promoting the pending migration into `prisma/migrations/` and flipping `prisma/schema.prisma` must ship together, and the flip is impossible while the shared committed provider is `sqlite`:
  - the CI `migrations` job ends with `prisma migrate diff --from-url "$DATABASE_URL" --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --exit-code`; a promoted migration that makes columns `numeric` while the schema still says `String` (→ `text`) reddens every CI run,
  - with `amount Decimal` under provider=sqlite, i128 values round-trip as `REAL` (measured, recorded in the plan doc) and `@db.Decimal` is rejected by `prisma validate` under that provider — the whole 395-test SQLite suite is the guard rail there.
  The decision is (a) re-platform dev/CI to Postgres (issue #14) then flip + `git mv` + delete the SQLite branch, (b) maintain a second committed Postgres schema, or (c) keep `String` in the shared schema and make exact `::numeric` casts (this PR's pattern) the permanent story. This PR is compatible with all three.

## Changes Made

- `src/routes/health.ts` — the two JS BigInt sums in `GET /stats` (`.reduce((acc, v) => acc + BigInt(v.amount), 0n)` for `settledValue` and the `.reduce(... BigInt(v.settledFee ?? '0'), 0n)` for `feesCollected`, plus `settledVouchers: settled.length`), which fetched **every** settled voucher to add up decimal strings in the process, move behind a new module-level `settledTotals()`. On Postgres (`isPostgres` from the existing `src/lib/database.ts`, same branching pattern as `src/routes/providers.ts:33`) one aggregate answers count and both sums in the database:
  ```sql
  SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS "settledVouchers",
         COALESCE(SUM("amount"::numeric), 0)::text AS "settledValue",
         COALESCE(SUM("settledFee"::numeric), 0)::text AS "feesCollected"
  FROM "Voucher" WHERE "status" = 'Settled'
  ```
  `numeric` is arbitrary-precision, so the sums are exact for every i128 the chain can produce. The `::numeric` cast is valid on today's `text` columns and a no-op on `numeric`, so **this query needs no edit when the pending migration is promoted**. Strings remain at the API boundary (base-unit decimal strings, unchanged response shape). On SQLite the BigInt pass stays verbatim: SQLite integer arithmetic caps at 2^63−1 and promotes overflow to float64, so a SQL sum there would be inexact for exactly the values these columns exist to hold — a correctness regression the issue cannot be asking for.
- `src/__tests__/routes.test.ts` — **no existing test modified.** One new test in the existing `GET /health and /stats` suite pins the invariant: a settled voucher with the i128 max amount (`340282366920938463463374607431768211455`) sums through `/stats` exactly.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — entry under Unreleased/Changed.
- `docs/amount-numeric-migration-plan.md` — the "what stays unchanged" and follow-up step 4 sections amended to match shipped reality (Postgres sums now run in SQL; step 4 says exactly what to delete at promotion).

## What breaks if this change is wrong

Only `GET /stats` totals on a Postgres deployment, and only if the raw
aggregate is wrong: every settled voucher with a non-numeric amount would
error the cast loudly (Postgres rejects `'abc'::numeric`; the pending
migration's preflight regex `^[+-]?[0-9]+$` documents the same invariant).
SQLite — every test, dev, and the docker quick start — is bit-for-bit
unchanged.

## How this was verified (actual runs, Node 22 / npm 9.2)

- Baseline on clean `origin/main` (`dfb933c`): `npm run lint` exit 0 · `npm run typecheck` exit 0 · `npm test` **394 passed / 28 files**, exit 0.
- After the change: `npm run lint` exit 0 · `npm run typecheck` exit 0 · `npm test` **395 passed / 28 files** (the 394 existing tests unchanged and green, plus the new one), exit 0.
- The new test run by name: `vitest run src/__tests__/routes.test.ts -t "i128-max"` → `✓ GET /health and /stats > sums a settled i128-max amount into settledValue exactly`, 1 passed. It passes on `main` too — it is a regression guard for the exactness property, not new-to-SQLite behaviour.
- **Postgres branch against a real Postgres 18.4** (throwaway embedded instance, outside the repo; not CI — CI has no Postgres route-test job until #14 lands): with `text` columns, the exact aggregate above returned `340282366920938463463392621830307693443` / `18014398509881989` / `4` matching BigInt ground truth including i128-max and 2^54-class fees; identical results after applying the pending migration's `ALTER ... SET DATA TYPE numeric` statements; empty table → `0` / `'0'` / `'0'`.

items.title: Fix issues: 865, 867
items.body:
This PR resolves the following assigned issues:
- closes #865
- closes #867

## Changes Made

### #865 — `deposit`/`withdraw` no longer extend the instance TTL (regression of #281)

`PoolContract::deposit` and `PoolContract::withdraw` (`contracts/pool/src/lib.rs`) were the only
LP-facing state-changing entrypoints that never bumped the contract instance TTL — the calls were
lost when share minting/burning was refactored into the `_mint`/`_burn` helpers. A pool whose
activity is exclusively deposits and withdrawals lets the instance entry (admin, contract wiring,
all totals) lapse toward expiry even while LPs use it daily.

- `deposit` now calls `Self::extend_instance_ttl(&env)` on the success path
  (`contracts/pool/src/lib.rs`, after the `lp_deposited` event).
- `withdraw` now calls `Self::extend_instance_ttl(&env)` on the success path
  (after the `lp_withdrawn` event).
  Same shared policy as every other entrypoint (`TTL_THRESHOLD` / `TTL_EXTEND_TO` from
  `trusttrove-ttl`), placed directly in the two entrypoints rather than in `_mint`/`_burn` so
  `transfer`/`transfer_from` (which already bump via `move_shares`'s callers) are not double-bumped
  needlessly — matching the acceptance criteria's "directly" option.

Red-first evidence (tests written and run BEFORE the fix):

```
test test::test_deposit_extends_instance_ttl_after_ledger_drain ... FAILED
  panicked: "deposit should extend instance ttl close to EXTEND_TO, got 50"
test test::test_withdraw_extends_instance_ttl_after_ledger_drain ... FAILED
  panicked: "withdraw should extend instance ttl close to EXTEND_TO, got 50"
```

The new tests drive the instance TTL below `TTL_THRESHOLD` with a ledger jump (keeping the mock
token's own entries alive across the jump — they carry the default ~4096-ledger TTL), then assert
the entrypoint bumps the instance back near `EXTEND_TO`. Pre-existing suite untouched, including
`test_deposit_extends_instance_ttl_when_below_threshold` (which only exercises `initialize`).

### #867 — escrow `initialize` emits no event

`invoice`/`registry` emit `contract_initialized` and `pool` emits `pool_initialized`, but
`EscrowContract::initialize` published nothing, so indexers following escrow deployments could not
see the admin, pool and funding asset without reading storage.

- Added `contract_initialized(env, admin, pool_contract, usdc_asset)` to
  `contracts/escrow/src/events.rs` (symbol + three address topics, `()` data — the invoice naming
  and format convention).
- `initialize` calls it at the end, after the instance TTL bump
  (`contracts/escrow/src/lib.rs`), mirroring pool's ordering.
- New test `test_initialize_emits_contract_initialized_event` asserts the event is published from
  the escrow contract with the configured admin, pool and asset as topics.

Red-first evidence (test run BEFORE the fix):

```
test test::test_initialize_emits_contract_initialized_event ... FAILED
  panicked: "initialize must publish a contract_initialized event"
```

- `docs/EVENTS.md`: Escrow section now documents `contract_initialized` in the existing table format.

## Verification (real numbers)

- Baseline at `main` (`8102d0e`), unmodified tree:
  - `cargo test -p trusttrove-pool -p trusttrove-escrow` → pool **235 passed / 0 failed**, escrow
    **77 passed / 0 failed** (+ doc-test runs, exit 0).
- After the fixes (re-run on the exact committed tree, post `cargo fmt`):
  - pool **237 passed / 0 failed** (+2 = the two new #865 tests), escrow **78 passed / 0 failed**
    (+1 = the new #867 test). Exit 0.
- CI gates from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `cargo fmt --all --check` → clean;
  `cargo clippy -p trusttrove-pool -p trusttrove-escrow --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
  → clean.

## Honest caveats

- In this clone environment, any `cargo test` run regenerates ~114 committed
  `test_snapshots/*.json` goldens (local soroban-sdk formatting drift). All regenerated goldens were
  reverted before committing; the three new goldens produced by the new tests are covered by the

items.body:
Closes #60

---

This PR is a **partial delivery** against https://github.com/Godgift-care/sci-healthcare-backend/issues/60 and deliberately carries no `closes` line.

Addresses the migration-plan criterion of https://github.com/Godgift-care/sci-healthcare-backend/issues/60; the remaining criteria require a maintainer decision on Postgres dev/CI, recorded on the issue.

## Changes

- `prisma/postgres-pending/20260107000000_amount_numeric_to_decimal/migration.sql` — hand-written, Postgres-targeted conversion of the i128-as-string amount columns (`Voucher.amount` / `Voucher.settledNet` / `Voucher.settledFee`, `Receipt.amount`, `FaucetDrip.amount`, plus `Service.price` and `ServicePriceChange.price`, which `schema.prisma` documents as the same i128-as-decimal-string class) to **plain `numeric`, not `numeric(65,30)`**: a `(p,s)` column allows `p−s` = 35 integer digits, but i128 ranges to 39 digits, and stroop amounts have no fixed fractional scale. Includes a preflight `DO` block that names any non-decimal-integer rows per column before touching them (mirroring the guarded backfill in `20260106000000_voucher_seq`).
- `docs/amount-numeric-migration-plan.md` — the full plan: what the SQL does and why it is pending, the inverse statements (kept out of the migration file), deploy/locking notes, and the exact follow-up sequence once maintainers adopt a Postgres dev/CI service (schema `Decimal` → `toString()` at `serialise()` / `formatReceipt()` → SQL `_sum` replacing the BigInt loops in `src/routes/health.ts:170-180` and `src/routes/receipts.ts:145-146,186-200` → native `orderBy` retiring `pageByAmount`, `src/routes/vouchers.ts:454-489`).
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Unreleased/Added entry. The repo has no PR-title lint guard (checked `.github/workflows/`), so the title is a plain Conventional Commit.

**Why the SQL is NOT under `prisma/migrations/` yet** (the CI-consistency check this PR ran before pushing): the `migrations` job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:64-94`, README "Schema changes and migrations") applies every folder in `prisma/migrations/` to a fresh Postgres via `prisma migrate deploy`, then runs `prisma migrate diff --from-url "$DATABASE_URL" --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --exit-code` and fails on any drift. `schema.prisma` is committed with `provider = "sqlite"` and `String` amounts (which map to `text`), so a shipped migrations folder converting these columns to `numeric` would make the drift check non-empty and break every CI run — the migration and the schema flip must land in the same change, and the schema flip is exactly the Postgres dev/CI decision that belongs to the maintainers (recorded on the issue; see also the measured SQLite evidence in the plan doc: a `Decimal` amount round-trips as `REAL` above 2^53 on SQLite). `prisma/postgres-pending/` is read by nothing; when the decision lands it is a `git mv` plus the schema edit.

## Not changed

`prisma/schema.prisma`, anything under `src/`, the SQLite dev/test default, `migration_lock.toml`, and CI config. No runtime behavior changes in this PR.

## Verification (all through the machine's memory-bounded sandbox runner)

- Baseline at `6e911d6` and after this diff, identical results (the gate run at `6e911d6` began on the pristine worktree; the few doc/SQL files added mid-run are not read by any gate — `eslint src`, `tsc -p tsconfig.json`, vitest `include: src/**/*.test.ts` — so both sides are equivalent, and the after-run below executed against the committed tree):
  - `npm ci` — exit 0 at baseline (no lockfile change, tree identical after)
  - `npm run lint` — exit 0 (both)
  - `npm run typecheck` — exit 0 (both)
  - `npm test` (vitest) — baseline at `6e911d6`: **26 files / 364 tests passed (364)**, exit 0; with this diff: **26 files / 364 tests passed (364)**, exit 0 — identical both sides (real test names observed in both runs; e.g. `✓ src/__tests__/indexer.test.ts (21 tests)`).
  - `npx prisma validate` — exit 0 with this diff (`DATABASE_URL` provided in the shell; the schema is untouched and `prisma` reads nothing from `prisma/postgres-pending/`).
- The migration SQL itself was **not executed**: there is no Postgres on this machine and I did not install one or use Docker, so the CI `migrations` job cannot be replicated locally. The drift-gate conclusion above is derived from `ci.yml:89-94` and README:631-639, which fully determine the failure mode. Stated plainly so nobody mistakes this for a migrate-deploy-tested migration.

This PR resolves the following assigned issues:

## Summary

`/compare` was unreachable from any link and hard-limited to three time
windows, and a malformed id in the shared `?ids=` URL failed the whole
comparison silently. This adds the two entry points the issue asks for,
supports the full window set, validates ids on the server component with a
visible note for what was dropped, and covers all of it with tests.

## Changes Made

**Entry points**
- `apps/web/app/(app)/contracts/ContractsClient.tsx` — the bulk-actions
  toolbar (which already carries per-row checkboxes from #176) grows a
  **Compare** action: with ≥2 contracts selected it renders a real
  `<a id="bulk-compare-btn" href="/compare?ids=…">` carrying the whole
  selection in the shared URL (the compare page caps the view at four and
  says so); below that it renders an inert disabled button.
- `apps/web/app/(app)/contracts/[id]/page.tsx` — the detail page header

**All windows**
- `apps/web/app/(app)/compare/page.tsx` — `SUPPORTED_WINDOWS` is now the
  full `TimeWindow` set (`24h/7d/30d/all`); `parseWindow` accepts `all`.
- `apps/web/components/compare/CompareView.tsx` — the window selector
  drops its three-window subset and uses the app-wide set. Because
  `GET /api/v1/compare` only aggregates the documented 24h/7d/30d (unknown
  values are silently normalised to 24h in `apps/api/internal/handler/compare.go`),
  the **All** window is assembled client-side rather than relabelling 24h
  data as lifetime totals:
- `apps/web/lib/compareAll.ts` (new) — builds the same
  `CompareContractEntry` shape from the endpoints that already expose
  lifetime data: overall totals from `getContractStats` (the same mapping

  untracked/zeroed entry, per-entry stats outage, health 404 vs failure,

  for all four windows and the fallback.
- `apps/web/components/compare/CompareView.test.tsx` (+4 tests) — all
  four window buttons render; clicking **All** goes through
  `getCompareAllEntries` and never asks the API for `window=all`; null
  averages render "—"; the invalid-id and truncation notes appear.
- `apps/web/app/(app)/contracts/page.test.tsx` (+1 test) — Compare is
  inert at one selection and at two becomes
  `/compare?ids=A,B` carrying both ids.

items.title: Fix issue: 236
items.body:
This PR resolves the following assigned issues:
- closes #236

## Relationship to sibling PR #249 and issue #235

This PR deliberately does **not** touch `src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx` or
`src/app/(dashboard)/agents/page.tsx`, which open sibling PR #249 is editing for the section-level
error-boundary work in #235. There is no file overlap with #249.

On the page-level acceptance criteria of #235: `main` already ships a route-level dashboard error
boundary at `src/app/(dashboard)/error.tsx` (a Next App Router `error.tsx` with a "Try again"
`reset()` trigger and a clean `console.error` log), plus `src/app/global-error.tsx` at the root.
The finer-grained *widget-section* boundaries (wallets / policies / agent monitors) named in the
#235 description are exactly what #249 implements, so this PR adds no competing second boundary
class; #236 is carried here on its own.

## Changes Made

**`src/components/ui/dialog.tsx`** — hardened keyboard navigation and the focus trap in the shared
`Dialog` modal primitive, so every consumer dialog benefits (agent/asset creation
`AddAssetDialog`, transaction confirmation `TransactionSigningModal`,
`ProposalApprovalConfirmDialog`, `BudgetAllocationModal`, `SignerManagement`, `CredentialVault`,
`RBACManagementView`, `SignerThresholdConfig`, `AuditTimeline`, `CircuitBreakerConfirmModal`,
`TransactionDetailDrawer`, `FeeOptimizationPanel`, `BudgetBreakdownChart` — ~15 call sites).

Gaps fixed (each was reachable from `main`):

1. **Leaky focus trap.** The old `Tab` handler only wrapped when `document.activeElement` was
   *exactly* the first or last focusable. If focus drifted outside the panel (e.g. clicking static
   dialog text focuses `body`; Shift+Tab from the panel itself), the browser's default tab order
   walked straight through the background page. Now: any `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` while focus is outside
   the panel is intercepted and pulled back in (`first` on Tab, `last` on Shift+Tab); Shift+Tab
   from the panel wraps to the last focusable; with no focusables inside, focus stays pinned to
   the panel.
2. **Trap state corrupted by unstable `onClose`.** The trap effect had `onClose` in its dependency
   array, and every consumer passes a fresh inline arrow (`onClose={() => setOpen(false)}`). Each
   parent re-render therefore tore down the listener and re-ran the effect: re-capturing
   `document.activeElement` as the "trigger" (now an element *inside* the dialog — so focus
   restore on close went to the wrong place), calling `panelRef.current?.focus()` again (stealing
   focus from an input mid-typing whenever the dialog re-rendered), and re-locking body scroll.
   The effect now depends only on `[open]`; the latest `onClose` is kept in a ref. Trigger capture,
   initial focus, and scroll lock now happen exactly once per open transition.
3. **Disabled/hidden nodes stalled the cycle.** The focusable selector matched disabled buttons and
   hidden inputs, which cannot receive focus, so the wrap could silently break at the edges.
   Focusables are now filtered through an `isKeyboardFocusable` check (`disabled`,
   `aria-hidden`, `input[type=hidden]`, zero-size).
4. **Unguarded focus restore.** `previouslyFocused?.focus?.()` fired even when the trigger had
   unmounted with the panel that housed it; restore now only happens if the trigger is still
   connected to the document (and was not `body`).

Escape dismissal, overlay-click dismissal, `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, labelledby/
describedby wiring and the body scroll lock were already correct and are preserved. No new
dependencies — React + DOM APIs only, per the issue's own implementation guidance. No CI configs
or package manifests were touched.

## Verification (real output)

This repo has **no test runner** (0 test/spec files, no `test` script); CI is
build + typecheck + lint. I did not add one and I am not claiming any test pass. These are the
static-analysis gates I ran, in-sandbox (memory-capped cgroup), on pristine `main` first
(`1741e07`) and then on this branch (`8140164`):

```
$ npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit     — baseline on main: exit 0, no output
                        #                    branch: exit 0, no output
$ npm run lint          # next lint        — baseline on main: exit 0
✔ No ESLint warnings or errors              (branch: identical)
$ npm run build         # next build       — baseline on main: exit 0
                        #                    branch: exit 0, all 17 dashboard routes compiled,
                        #                    "First Load JS shared by all 87.4 kB" unchanged
```

`$ npm ci` — 486 packages, exit 0.

Manual behavioural checklist (verified by reading the keydown paths; this environment cannot run a
browser): Tab/Shift+Tab cycle stays inside the dialog including from a focus drift to `body`;
Escape closes; focus returns to the trigger element on close.

Fixes #236 (keyboard navigation + focus trap for modal dialogs).

items.title: fix(db): order vouchers by numeric id
items.body:
This PR resolves the following assigned issues:
- closes #61

### What changed

`Voucher.id` is the on-chain u64 kept as a **string**, so every `ORDER BY id` was
lexicographic: voucher `10` sorted before voucher `9` in the list page, in the keyset
cursor and in the CSV export. This adds a numeric ordering key and moves every
id-ordered read path onto it.

- **`prisma/schema.prisma`** — `Voucher` gains `seq BigInt?`, the numeric mirror of `id`.
  `BIGINT` rather than `Int` because the seeded id space alone starts at 9e12. It is never
  exposed by an API response.
- **`prisma/migrations/20260106000000_voucher_seq/migration.sql`** — adds the column and
  backfills existing rows from their id. The backfill is guarded (`id ~ '^[0-9]+$'` and a
  BIGINT range check) so a non-numeric or out-of-range id stays `NULL` instead of failing
  the migration.
- **`src/lib/voucher_seq.ts`** (new) — `voucherSeq(id)` returns the numeric value of a
  decimal id, or `null` for a hand-written label id (`bulk-0001`), an empty/negative id, or
  a value above the BIGINT range (u64 max). It is deliberately import-free so the seed
  script can use it without pulling in the environment contract.
- **`src/stellar/indexer.ts`** — the `voucher_created` handler writes `seq: voucherSeq(id)`
  when it creates the row. The replay branch is `update: {}`, so a replayed event leaves the
  stored `seq` alone rather than blanking it.
- **`src/routes/vouchers.ts`** — a new `idOrder(order)` helper returns
  `[{ seq: { sort, nulls: 'last' } }, { id: order }]` and is used by `pageByWhere`,
  `pageByAmount` and `voucherCsv`. The string `id` is kept as the final tie-break so rows
  with no `seq` still have one deterministic order. `nulls: 'last'` holds in both
  directions, so the unnumbered tail cannot fall between two pages.
  The **keyset cursor** had to change with the ordering: a keyset predicate must compare the
  columns it orders by, so it now reads the cursor row's own `seq` (one `findUnique` by
  primary key, falling back to `voucherSeq(decoded.id)` if the cursor outlives its row) and
  builds an `(createdAt, seq, id)` predicate with a separate branch for a `NULL`-`seq` cursor.
- **`src/scripts/seed.ts`** — seeded rows write the same `seq` mirror, so seeded and indexed
  rows sort alike.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** — entry under Unreleased → Fixed.

What breaks if this is wrong: pagination can repeat or drop a row at a page boundary when two
vouchers share a `createdAt`, and the CSV export order stops matching the list order.

### Evidence

Test command is this repo's own `npm test`, which is `vitest run` (`vitest.config.ts` →
`include: ['src/**/*.test.ts']`, `setupFiles: ['./test/env.ts']`, throwaway SQLite db created
by `test/global-setup.ts` via `prisma db push`). Test names and counts below are the real
observed output.

**Baseline vs branch** (full `npm test`):

| state | result |
| --- | --- |
| `upstream/main` @ `905abeb` | **286 passed, 0 failed** (20 files) |
| this branch @ `ead03fa` | **299 passed, 0 failed** (21 files) |

No pre-existing failure was touched and no new failure added; the delta is exactly the 13
tests in `src/__tests__/voucher_seq.test.ts` (baseline ran from a separate clean worktree at
`upstream/main`, with its own `prisma generate`).

**Fail-without-fix proof.** Reverting only the source, keeping the tests:

1. Revert only the read-path ordering in `src/routes/vouchers.ts` to the base version
   (schema column, `voucherSeq()` and the indexer write kept) → `6 failed | 7 passed`. The
   failures carry the bug's exact signature:
   - `GET /vouchers id ordering > returns voucher 9 before voucher 10 when sorting ascending`
     → `expected [ '10', '9' ] to deeply equal [ '9', '10' ]`
   - `... > uses the numeric id as the tie-break for the expiresAt sort too` → same inversion
   - `... > pages 9 and 10 into separate pages instead of repeating or dropping one`
     → `expected [ '9' ] to deeply equal [ '10' ]`
   - `... > still orders hand-made rows without a numeric id deterministically`
     → `expected [ '10', '9', 'bulk-0001', 'bulk-0002' ] to deeply equal [ '9', '10', ... ]`
   - `GET /vouchers.csv id ordering > lists voucher 9 before voucher 10` → same inversion
   - `... > returns voucher 10 before voucher 9 when sorting descending` → inverted too
   The 7 that still pass are the ones that don't depend on the read path
   (`voucherSeq` unit tests, `seq` column/handler tests), which is the expected split.
2. Additionally revert the write path in `src/stellar/indexer.ts` → `8 failed | 5 passed`,
   now including `voucher_created handler > fills seq from the voucher id` and
   `... > backfills seq when a replayed event recreates the row`.
3. Restore both files → `voucher_seq.test.ts` **13 passed (13)**, and the full suite back to
   299/299.

**Other gates** — all three are defined by the repo and all pass on this branch, identical to
baseline:

- `npm run lint` (`eslint src`) → exit 0
- `npm run typecheck` (`tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`) → exit 0 (after `npx prisma generate`)
- `npm run build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.json`) → exit 0

Tests covering the acceptance criteria: `voucherSeq > mirrors a decimal id as its numeric
value`, `> is null for an id with no numeric value, or one past the column range`,
`> orders 9 before 10 where the string id orders 10 first`, the `voucher_created handler`
trio, the `GET /vouchers id ordering` suite (asc, desc, `expiresAt` sort, page boundary,
`seq` kept out of the response, deterministic `NULL`-`seq` tail) and the CSV test — i.e. ids
9 and 10 as specified.

### Not verified locally

- **The Postgres migration path was not exercised on this machine** (no Postgres installed), so `scripts/use-postgres.sh` + `npx prisma migrate deploy` and the `prisma migrate diff --from-url "$DATABASE_URL" --to-schema-datamodel prisma/schema.prisma --exit-code` step could not be reproduced locally. Note that the test suite builds its database with `prisma db push` against SQLite and therefore does **not** execute `migration.sql` at all -- a green `npm test` is not evidence that the migration applies. It has since been confirmed by the repo's own CI: the `migrations` job (Postgres 16) and `test`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `build` and `auto-merge bot tests` are all **pass** on this PR. - SQLite, not Postgres, backs every test run reported above.
- No index was added for `seq`. The existing composites from #58 (`(funder, createdAt)`,
  `(funder, expiresAt)`, …) still cover the filter plus the primary sort key; `seq` is only the
  tie-break. Adding `seq` to those composites would be a measurable change that needs `EXPLAIN
  ANALYZE` on Postgres, which is not available here, so it is left out rather than guessed at.
- No API response gained or lost a field, so `docs/developers/api.md` (contracts repo) needs no
  change; `CHANGELOG.md` was updated. No dependencies changed, so no lockfile churn.

### Post-creation update

All CI checks on this PR are **pass** (`test`, `lint`, `typecheck`,
`build`, `migrations`, CodeQL, `auto-merge bot tests`). The `migrations` job is the
first real execution of `20260106000000_voucher_seq` against Postgres 16, including the
`migrate diff --exit-code` schema-drift guard, so the caveat above is now closed.

Branch: `fix/voucher-seq-and-amounts` (1 commit ahead of `main`, 0 behind), opened against
`main`.

items.title: fix(invoice): extend instance TTL on pool/agent-registry setter update paths (#864)
items.body:
This PR resolves the following assigned issues:
- closes #864

## Changes Made

**`contracts/invoice/src/lib.rs`** — in `set_pool_contract` and `set_agent_registry_contract`, the `Self::extend_instance_ttl(&env)` call sat inside the `else` branch of the `if let Some(old) = ...` (the "no previous value" path), so re-pointing the pool or agent-registry address on an already-initialised instance skipped the instance-TTL bump and left the instance entry to expire. Both setters now call `Self::extend_instance_ttl(&env)` unconditionally after the storage `set` and before the event branch — the exact shape already used by `set_escrow_contract`. The bump goes through the existing `extend_instance_ttl` helper (`TTL_THRESHOLD` / `TTL_EXTEND_TO` from the shared `trusttrove-ttl` crate); no new constants, errors, or events were added. The first-set event payloads are untouched (that is #430's scope).

**`contracts/invoice/src/test.rs`** — two regression tests, in the style of the pool crate's `test_deposit_extends_instance_ttl_when_below_threshold`:
- `test_set_pool_contract_replacement_extends_instance_ttl`
- `test_set_agent_registry_contract_replacement_extends_instance_ttl`

Each performs a first set (bumps the instance TTL to ~`TTL_EXTEND_TO`), advances the ledger so the remaining instance TTL drops below `TTL_THRESHOLD` (asserted before the update call), then calls the setter again with a new address and asserts the instance TTL was refreshed to at least `TTL_THRESHOLD`, plus that the stored address was actually replaced. Verified against the unfixed `lib.rs`: both tests fail with "should extend the instance ttl, got 100000"; with the fix they pass. items.title: test(escrow): fix issues 111, 122, 124, 125
items.body:
This PR resolves the following assigned issues:
- closes #111
- closes #122
- closes #124
- closes #125

### Changes Made

**#111 — exact deadline-boundary tests for `advance1_deadline` / `advance2_deadline` (`contracts/escrow/tests/deadline_boundary.rs`, 12 tests + `tests/common/mod.rs`).**
I read the operators in the code before writing anything, and they are already correct complements: `claim_tranche` rejects on `env.ledger().timestamp() > tranche_deadline(...)` → **`Error::ClaimWindowPassed`**, so the deadline instant itself is still claimable; `reclaim_tranche` rejects on `timestamp <= tranche_deadline(...)` → **`Error::ClaimWindowNotPassed`**, so reclaim first becomes possible at `deadline + 1`. So there is no overlap, no gap, and no off-by-one to fix — the doc comments were the inaccurate part ("if within the window" never said who owns the boundary instant), and `claim_window_secs`'s field doc now states the inclusive/exclusive convention plus the consequence nobody had written down: the cooperative's effective window spans `claim_window_secs + 1` distinct timestamps. The tests pin, per tranche: claim exactly at the deadline succeeds, claim one tick past fails with `ClaimWindowPassed`, reclaim exactly at the deadline fails with `ClaimWindowNotPassed`, reclaim one tick past succeeds; plus two cross-cutting invariants — the deadline instant belongs to claim and never to reclaim, and no timestamp ever admits both parties or neither — and that a boundary rejection surfaces the deadline error rather than a state error.

**#122 — Address-vs-Address equality audit (`contracts/escrow/tests/address_equality.rs`, 7 tests + `docs/address-equality-audit.md`).**
Audit result: **no stringly-typed comparison exists, so there is nothing to fix.** Every auth decision is delegated to `Address::require_auth()` (host-enforced over the auth entry's address value); the only two hand-written comparisons are `flag_dispute`'s `NotAParty` chain (`flagger != c.buyer && flagger != c.cooperative && flagger != c.warehouse_operator`) and `require_once_each`'s dedup (`addresses[..i].iter().all(|seen| seen != addr)`), both of which use `soroban_sdk::Address: PartialEq`, evaluated by the host over the canonical `ScAddress` value. Token transfers and `settle` use addresses only as keys. `lib.rs` is `#![no_std]`, never converts an `Address` through `to_string`/`to_strkey`/`format!`/bytes, and `BytesN<32>` appears only as `AllocationMember::member_hash`, compared nowhere. The suite makes the finding re-runnable: value equality survives a `Val`/`ScAddress` round trip, distinct addresses stay unequal (including prefix-confusable ones), `flag_dispute` accepts a party passed as a *different object* than the stored one, `NotAParty` rejects an unrelated address, membership follows `reassign_buyer` by value, and `require_once_each` dedups by value — plus `lib_source_never_stringifies_addresses`, a source-level guard in the same spirit as `.github/scripts/check_error_discriminants.sh` that fails if a string-conversion token ever reappears in `lib.rs` while asserting the two legitimate comparisons are still present.

**#124 — Reflector oracle fault-injection harness (`contracts/escrow/tests/oracle_fault_injection.rs`, 12 tests).**
An inline mock callee (repo integration-test conventions: `#[contract]` module + the shared `tests/common/mod.rs` world) drives ten fault modes at the only two outbound calls in the contract: no config, no quote on record, stale quote, quote exactly at the staleness bound, a `panic!`ing callee, an unreachable callee (address with nothing deployed), a future-dated quote, a negative price, a price that overflows the conversion multiply, and a garbage `decimals()`. The documented degradation is real and asserted: `OracleNotConfigured` on both `oracle_rate` and `resolve_fx_shortfall`, `OraclePriceUnavailable` when the oracle returns `None` for the asset, `OracleStale` past `max_age_secs` (inclusive at the bound), and a fault never yields a successful-but-wrong value or a partial write. The `OracleNotConfigured` doc comment now names both readers. **Four findings are pinned as current behavior with `FINDING` markers rather than silently fixed**, because each fix changes settlement math or the public error surface and needs a product decision: **F1** an unreachable oracle aborts at the host — no catchable contract error, and `oracle_config` has no setter, so the commitment is permanently unreadable; **F2** `now.saturating_sub(quote.timestamp)` gives a future-dated quote age `0`, so it passes the staleness bound for as long as the ledger stays behind it (a `u64::MAX` stamp passes forever); **F3** a negative price is returned unvalidated and a negative `fx_adjusted_total` clamps the shortfall to `0`, so `settle()` pays the cooperative nothing further and refunds the escrow — one bad oracle value inverts who the settlement favors; **F4/F5** `ngn_owed * rate.price` and `10i128.pow(decimals)` are unchecked, so a huge price or a garbage decimals count aborts resolution.

**#125 — snapshot-based regression replay (`contracts/escrow/tests/snapshot_replay.rs`, 4 tests + 8 fixtures + `tests/fixtures/README.md`).**
Format: line-oriented, dependency-free `key = value` transcripts under `contracts/escrow/tests/fixtures/*.snap` — terms as fields, `step = <call> [args...] => ok | err(ErrorVariant)` for ledger calls, `step = advance <secs>` / `set_time <ts>` for clock moves, `check = <key> <value>` for recorded balances/statuses replayed *in transcript order* (a recorded balance belongs to a point in the sequence, not to its end). No `serde`/`serde_json` dependency was added. The loader parses the whole directory and panics with `file:line` on a malformed line, and it is itself under test (`fixtures_are_present_named_and_sourced`) so a fixture with no name, no provenance, no steps or no checks cannot pass by accident. **Data provenance, stated plainly:** `HANDOFF.md` records ten deployments with contract ids, WASM hashes and the figures read back off the ledger, but **not a single transaction envelope XDR, auth-entries XDR or ledger export** — and it calls the instances "validation artifacts, not infrastructure". So this is a replay of *recorded chain outcomes*, not recorded chain bytes; nothing here claims to be raw chain data, and every fixture's mandatory `provenance` line says which deployment it came from and how faithful it is. Coverage: Deployment 2 (pre-two-phase funding), Deployment 5 happy path / buyer default / seller non-delivery, Deployment 6 partial delivery + grade adjustment, Deployment 7 allocation ledger, Deployment 9's live GBP/USD FX top-up (the recorded `135300006985028` quote reproduces `fx_adjusted_total` 135,300,006 exactly) and Deployment 10's dispute freeze. **Real, actionable finding:** the current build does not reproduce three recorded Deployment 2 outcomes — `confirm_delivery` succeeded from `Advance2Released` then and is `InvalidState` now; an out-of-order `settle` returned `Error(Contract, #12)` `TrancheUnresolved` on-chain but reports `InvalidState` now because the status gate sits ahead of the tranche gate (integrators branching on the recorded code will see a different error); and the recorded closing `settle`, which swept 650,000,000 and finished `Settled`, is unreachable without a funded remainder. These are declared with `known_divergence` lines that the replay asserts in **both** directions — today's build must still match the annotation *and* must still differ from the record — so a divergence can neither be papered over nor quietly go stale, while an undeclared one fails the job. `the_recorded_divergences_are_still_divergences` also pins the set itself (exactly 3, all from that deployment), and `the_recorded_dispute_freeze_rejection_is_still_a_rejection` re-asserts Deployment 10's live on-chain `InvalidState` directly.

**CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`).** Four new jobs — `deadline-boundary`, `address-equality`, `oracle-fault-injection`, `snapshot-replay` — each running one `cargo test --test <name>` in `contracts/escrow` so a failure names the issue it guards; `snapshot-replay` runs with `--nocapture` to print the replay report and the divergence list. The existing four jobs (`cargo test`, `stellar contract build`, `check-error-discriminants`, `check-auth-docs`) are untouched, and the new jobs reuse the same cargo cache key.

### Verification

```
cd contracts/escrow && cargo test
```

Exit 0, **167 tests, 0 failures** on Rust 1.98 / `soroban-sdk` 28.0.0: 134 existing unit tests (unchanged and green after the doc-comment edits), plus `deadline_boundary` 12/12, `address_equality` 7/7, `oracle_fault_injection` 12/12, `snapshot_replay` 4/4. Both CI guard scripts still pass: `bash .github/scripts/check_error_discriminants.sh` → `ok: Error discriminants 1..36 sequential` (no variant renumbered), `bash .github/scripts/check_auth_docs.sh` → `ok: all 29 public method doc comments name their required auth party`. No production logic changed — the diff to `src/lib.rs` is doc comments only — and no new crate dependency was added. Local CI jobs could not be executed here, so the four new job definitions are validated by YAML parse plus the exact commands run locally above.

items.body:
## Why this PR exists

Ademola chose option A for the Framer account (Free now, paid at launch). Turning that into a repo change surfaced one fact nobody had written down, and it is a trap:

items.title: P-19: register lists exact tokens (R-4 grep input)
items.body:
## Why this matters

`R-4` is the content gate: no placeholder, nothing unverified, no empty section visible at launch. Its input is `content/PLACEHOLDERS.md`, and it is planned as a grep against that table. A register that paraphrases is worse than an empty one, because the grep passes and everyone believes the gate ran.

Diffing the table against the files it claims to cover found three real mismatches, all in `content/demo-dataset.md`:

| Register said | The file actually says | Rows |
|---|---|---|
| `[One sentence...]` | `[One sentence]` and `[One sentence: what was made and for whom]` | 8 demo rows, two variants |
| nothing | `[Wedding name]` | `demo-wedding-1`, `demo-wedding-2` |

items.title: L-4: data protection duties researched, privacy and cookie copy drafted
items.body:
## What this is

L-4 (Privacy notice page and consent text; check NDPA 2023 duties) is the only Must task in the whole roadmap with a `none` dependency that was not blocked on Emmanuel and not blocked on a Framer account, so I took it. It is now `[~]`, not `[x]`: the research and the drafting are done, and the legal sign-off is not.

I read the operative instrument rather than summaries: the Commission's **NDP Act General Application and Implementation Directive (GAID) 2025**, 117 pages, from ndpc.gov.ng. That matters because GAID **repeals the NDPR 2019**, so most checklists and vendor "NDPR compliance" pages on the internet describe rules that are no longer in force, including the "30 days to answer a request" figure people still quote.

## Two live conflicts with this repo's own docs

Both are registered as tasks. Neither was silently fixed.

1. **Retention.** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` section 8 keeps a non-spam enquiry for **24 months** and spam for 30 days. GAID's storage-limitation article sets a default of **six calendar months** once the purpose is done, and its contract article says that where the contract did not materialise the data "shall be destroyed within six (6) months unless there is a justifiable ground to archive". An enquiry that never became a booking is exactly that case, so section 8 is probably wrong and has no recorded justification. **This is task L-7.** I did not edit section 8: a data model and retention change is an ask-first item under AGENTS.md, and "justifiable ground" is a decision for the owner and a lawyer, not for me.
2. **No cookie consent anywhere.** FR-21, P-16 and L-5 all plan GA4, and no doc in this repo requires a consent step for it. GAID requires an explicit yes/no for anything but strictly necessary cookies, and says a notice parked at the bottom of a page where it can be ignored "is tantamount to lack of transparency"; it must obstruct the middle, left or right of the home page. So Phase 0 shipping GA4 means shipping a banner, or not shipping GA4. **This is task L-6**, and it needs a new ESSENTIALS rule, which is an ask-first change, so it needs you.

A third finding got no task of its own: section 8 has no breach path, where the Act wants notice to the Commission within 72 hours and to affected people immediately. Phase 0 stores nothing and the Worker is conditional on G1, so handling is B-section work; writing the obligation is folded into L-7 and the owner's side into R-2.

## What I did write

- **`docs/research/ndpa-2023-notes.md`** (new, the bulk of this PR). Thresholds (5,000 / 1,000 / the 200-subject sensitive-data trigger), the Article 7 duties that apply at any size, the ten-item notice list, the consent rules, retention, rights, breach, processors and cross-border, penalties. Every claim carries the paragraph to check and a state: Certain, Likely, Guessing. Section 13 is the seven decisions that need a professional read, and the file closes by saying "NDPA compliant" is not a sentence for the pitch or the footer until those are answered.
  - Where the GAID font encoding mangled an article number I cite the article by name instead of inventing a number. The Act's own PDF at placng.gov.ng is a scanned image with no text layer and cert.gov.ng sits behind a Cloudflare challenge, so the sensitive-data definition, the under-18 rule and the penalty figures are labelled secondary source and need the Act text.
- **`content/copy.md`**: a privacy notice drafted item by item against the ten required contents, a cookie notice that shows on load with Accept and Reject as equal choices and is explicitly not in the footer, and a footer link. **Nine brackets**, all registered. I left the form's existing consent line alone because copy.md is declared the source of truth for `framer/EnquiryForm.tsx` and changing that string means touching the component in the same change.
- **`content/PLACEHOLDERS.md`**: seven new rows (six genuinely new tokens plus `[Confirm the trading name]`, which was only registered as a deck token and is now site copy too). Verified both directions: all twelve distinct brackets in copy.md are in the register, and every register row that claims copy.md matches it.
- **Q14** in the tracker and the question sheet: two numbers, how many records the business holds and how much of the publishable footage is at a church, mosque, festival or family ceremony where faith or ethnicity shows. Those two decide the tier. It is the sharpest exposure in this project, because the answer may be "yes, constantly", and that is a different compliance world from a booking form with names and phone numbers.
- **Docs consistency**: PRD section 9's `[verify obligations]` marker now points at the note and the four tasks instead of sitting unanswered; PRD section 5's In v1 list gained the notice page it never listed; ARCHITECTURE section 13 item 9 records that the reading happened and points at both conflicts; PROJECT_STRUCTURE gained the file in the tree and the table plus a Where-does-X-live row so no future agent reads the note as a fact base.

## Score: readiness goes down, and that is the correct result

Five Must tasks added (L-6, L-7, L-8, L-9, P-24). Must denominator 64 to 69, so readiness 19% to **17%**. Nothing was un-done; five duties nobody had written down are now written down.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Scorecard recomputed from the priority column of every row by parser | F 8/8, D 1/8, S 0/5, P 3/19, C 0/11, L 0/8, R 0/10, B 0/16 conditional, total **12 of 69**, Should 4 of 11 |
| Task row integrity | every row in F, D, S, P, C, L, R parses to exactly eight cells, no bad priority value, 0 malformed |
| Register agreement | 12 distinct brackets in copy.md, all registered; register rows claiming copy.md verified against it |
| Cross-references | L-6 to L-9, P-24, Q14, D-10 at fourteen, FR-21, FR-27, P-10, P-16, R-2, R-4, R-10, ESSENTIALS 8, PRD 9, ARCH 3, 8, 10, C-10, C-11 all resolve to real rows |
| `node --test` | 18 pass, 0 fail. Markdown-only change set, no code path touched |
| Em dashes | none in any changed file |

**Not checked, and it matters:** no legal verification of anything in the note. That is the whole reason L-4 stays `[~]`.

## Rules I did not break

No hard rule changed, no data model changed, no dependency added, no tooling installed (`pdftoppm` is missing here and installing it is an ask-first item, so the GAID text came out of two throwaway scripts in /tmp instead), no deploy, nothing published, no invented content. `/docs/research` is an input and is labelled that way in the file itself.

## After merge

1. You decide whether L-6 becomes an ESSENTIALS rule and whether Phase 0 runs GA4 at all.
2. Send Q14 with the rest of the sheet. Until those two numbers exist, L-9 cannot move and the notice stays bracketed.
3. Someone qualified reads `docs/research/ndpa-2023-notes.md` section 13. Nothing becomes a compliance claim before that.
4. Your PAT still has admin:org, delete:packages and workflow scope and is now in several transcripts. Rotate it.

items.body:
## What this closes

F-9 as written: "PRD section 10 says #0A0A0A, docs/DESIGN.md section 1 says #000000 and claims to replace it. One of them must change."

Picking a hex would have left the same class of bug in place. The two files each stated a value for the same fact, and nothing in the repo said which file was allowed to state it. So this PR settles ownership (ARCHITECTURE **decision D12**) rather than arguing about `#0A0A0A` versus `#000000`. Certain: DESIGN's black was already the value in the code (`framer/EnquiryForm.tsx:144`, `bg: "#000000"`), and every contrast ratio in DESIGN section 3 is measured against black, so `#000000` is what the project has actually been building toward.

## The conflict F-9 did not name

While reconciling section 10 I found a second, larger disagreement in the same three lines.

| | PRD section 10 said | DESIGN section 4 says |
|---|---|---|
| Display type | "Bold, clean sans-serif. Display font open (Syne is a candidate)" | a serif in the display role |

That is not a token drift, it is a visible change of direction for the whole site, and DESIGN.md made it unilaterally while describing itself as a draft whose colors came from sampling a logo file. **I did not resolve it.** Reverting DESIGN would be me choosing the look of the site; keeping it means Ademola signs off a direction the PRD never agreed to. So it is now **F-11** (owner Ademola, Should), and PRD section 10 names the supersession in place instead of hiding it. DESIGN section 13 item 4 was already the Framer check for it, now wired to P-1.

- **docs/PRD.md section 10**: states intent, carries no hex and no font name, and points at DESIGN sections 1, 3 and 4. The reference-site lesson bullet is untouched. Where the two disagree, DESIGN wins and this section gets corrected in the same change.
- **docs/DESIGN.md**: header line and section 1 now say it *holds the value* rather than *replaces the earlier PRD*, which was a claim about a file it does not own.
- **docs/ARCHITECTURE_ESSENTIALS.md**: one clause in the header line, the file agents read on every task, so the precedence is discoverable without opening three docs.

- **PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md**: framer/README.md:48 claims the design-token copy is called out under Known duplication. It was not. Added that bullet, a Where-does-X-live row for visual values, and a change log line. No file was added, moved or renamed.

Docs only, six files, no behavior change. The one sentence to check is D12: if you would rather PRD section 10 stay authoritative on look-and-feel, say so and I will invert it.

items.title: D-3: the deck asserted client facts it had no source for, plus a fix to PR #5
items.body:
## Contribution Protocol Checklist

- [x] I have updated the status of tasks in `ROADMAP.md`
- [x] I have recalculated the scorecard and Readiness line in `ROADMAP.md`
- [x] I have added a line to the Progress log in `ROADMAP.md`
- [x] I have updated `PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md` for any file/folder changes

## Description

The question sheet I merged in PR #5 made me go read my own pitch deck against the rule it enforces. Three of the deck's client facts came from the one file the repo forbids reading as fact.

### What the deck got wrong

AGENTS.md says never invent client names. `PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md` says `/docs/research` is never read as fact by an agent. And `docs/research/boy-concept-brief.md` has a header that says it directly:

> Do not copy numbers, names or registration details from here into the site, the CMS or **any pitch material**.

The deck is pitch material, and slide 4 asserted three things straight out of it:

| Deck said | Where it came from | Now says |
|---|---|---|
| `Alpha Movies Ltd (formerly Tue Tue Concept)` | brief line 7, no source anywhere else | `Alpha Movies Ltd (formerly [Confirm the trading name])` |
| `Instagram @alpha.movies_ and YouTube @Boy-concept` | brief lines 8 and 9 | `Instagram and YouTube [Confirm both handles]` |
| `One hero reel, silent hover previews, and a player...` | brief line 33, the reference layout note | `One hero reel, poster-first cards, and a player...` |

The handle is worse than unverified. The repo has `@alpha.movies_` and you quoted `alpha_movies_ltd` to me on 2026-10-10. Whichever is right, the deck currently prints the other one, in front of Emmanuel, on the slide that is supposed to make him look established. [Certain] that two candidates exist and neither has a verification-log row.

The hover previews are a different fault: the deck promised a feature ARCHITECTURE §9 and DESIGN §8 reject. Video is created on tap, autoplaying iframes are banned everywhere, and most visitors arrive from Instagram on a phone that has no hover. An agent copied a layout note from an unverified brief into a client-facing promise.

The deck did two things right and I left them alone: the RC number is bracketed rather than printing `9388573` from the brief, and there is no stats section at all, so "10M+ views" never reached it. [Certain], I scanned all 67 parts of the package for `10M`, `9388573`, `10M+`, `views`, `elite` and `world-class`.

Nothing was invented to fill the gaps. `[Confirm ...]` matches the convention slide 4 already used for `[Confirm on CAC public search]` and `[Confirm city]`. The three new tokens are registered in a new **Pitch material** section of `content/PLACEHOLDERS.md`, along with the deck's own `[YOUR NAME]`, `₦[amount]` x5, `[X]%` and `[X] weeks`, which are yours to fill and not the client's. Q13 in the tracker now asks the name and handle question.

### A fix to PR #5, which is on main

One edit in the question sheet failed and I did not catch it before merging. The answer map at the bottom keys on Q numbers, but Part 1 kept its original four columns, so the two disagreed on main. That also meant Q9 (will his team change the bio link and DM replies, which is what FR-25 depends on) and base city had no row at all. Part 1 now has the Q column, covers all twelve open questions, and adds Q13 as row 11. [Certain], checked by counting the rows and re-reading both tables.

This is my second silent-edit failure in this repo and both went through because I verified the file rather than the operation. If you want a stronger check than my reading, the CI gate would need a docs lint, which is a dependency decision, so I am flagging rather than doing it.

### How I edited a .pptx, and why not with the deck tool

The Presentations office engine read the deck fine and then refused every write with `QODER_OFFICE_PPTX_CONTENT_TYPES_INVALID`, and it reports `pageGenerationSupported: false` with a 1280 x 1809 canvas. So I edited the two slide parts inside the zip: extract, replace the string in the single `<a:t>` run, `zip` the entry back in. Every text block on a slide is one run, which is what makes string replacement safe here.

Verification, because a binary edit deserves more than a look:
- CRC and entry comparison against a copy of the original: 67 entries before and after, only `ppt/slides/slide4.xml` and `ppt/slides/slide6.xml` differ, and their compression method is the only other change. Everything else is byte-identical.
- Every XML and .rels part parses with no errors.
- `python zipfile.testzip()` returns no bad entry.
- Re-read through the office engine: it loaded the edited file from disk, shows the new text in the same boxes at the same font size, and returned an empty `audit` array, so no overflow or out-of-bounds was introduced.

Not checked: opening it in PowerPoint or Canva. Nothing here can do that, so treat "it will import cleanly" as [Likely] rather than verified. The file is 153 KB against 181 KB, which is re-deflate of unchanged entries, not lost content, and the CRC comparison is the evidence for that. The rule and the exact procedure are now written into `PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md` so the next agent does not rediscover it.

## Risk

- Slide 4 now reads as a deck with gaps in it. That is the honest state and D-3 turns them into values, but if you would rather the row disappear than show a bracket, that is a one-line change and your call.
- The former trading name is only worth printing if he confirms it. If "Tue Tue Concept" is real it is a nice bit of history, if it is wrong it is exactly the kind of detail that makes a pitch look careless.
- I did not touch the deck's layout, colors or fonts. The red `#C8102E` the deck uses is not a `docs/DESIGN.md` token, and F-9 is still open on the background color conflict. The deck predates the design system and reconciling them is P-1 and D-3 work, not this PR.

items.body:

## Description

Ademola's instruction was: for the work gated on Emmanuel, use placeholders that can be replaced later, or source videos from his Instagram. This PR does the first half in full and, on the second half, asks instead of scraping. Reasoning below.

Two new files, both docs, no code touched.

**`content/demo-dataset.md` (P-22)** is the CMS content the Phase 0 pages need, drafted with every client fact bracketed, so P-2, P-5, P-6, P-7, P-8 and P-10 stop being blocked by a man with a camera and a phone.
- SiteSettings: the six fields from ARCHITECTURE section 5, all bracketed. An empty field is left empty rather than guessed, because `EnquiryForm` has a designed path for an unset `whatsappDigits` (no handoff button, copyable brief plus the `[Enquiry Email]` line), so a placeholder number is strictly worse than none.
- Eight Project rows, two per FR-3 category, `slug` prefixed `demo-`, every row `verified: false` and `publish_ok: false`. Two per category is what makes the filter and the FR-26 empty-category hide rule testable; it is not a content bar, C-9 still sets that.
- Four Credential rows across the DESIGN section 7 type labels, each with a source column that is itself bracketed, because the source is the evidence.
- No stats row at all. A bracketed `[Amount] views` on a card reads as a lie with a gap in it, so C-6 either brings a source or the section shows none.
- An empty-poster treatment that obeys DESIGN section 9 (no stock, no AI stand-ins) using tokens from DESIGN section 3, and a DEMO badge that is deliberately not gold, since gold means "this matters or this is clickable".
- Seven-step flip-to-live, and two named routes for the one thing it needs decided.

**`pitch/emmanuel-question-sheet.md` (D-10)** is what converts the brackets. All twelve open questions ordered by how much they unblock, each mapped to the task it closes and the file that changes. A per-video table that collects client permission and music clearance in one pass instead of one argument at a time. A list of what counts as evidence per claim, so C-4 and C-5 arrive with sources attached. Part 4 is a five-question WhatsApp message Ademola can send now, so Emmanuel answers in two minutes from his phone.

### On sourcing videos from Instagram

I did not scrape the feed, and the site should not embed it. Not squeamishness about the tool, three concrete problems:

1. Downloading Instagram media is against their terms and the files are their CDN's. Links rot and the assets are not ours to ship into a pitch.
2. ARCHITECTURE section 3 already chose YouTube nocookie or Vimeo, created on tap. An Instagram embed inside a Framer code component inside the in-app browser adds a fourth unverified runtime to a list (section 13) that already has the one that blocks the design.
3. Permission cannot come from the feed. FR-27 needs his word per project, and Q8 needs the music answer. Weddings are private, and PRD risk 5 says a blocked track mid-play is a worse outcome than a shorter reel.

His own work is the right content, and he is the right person to grant permission for it. So the sheet asks him to post the four to six cuts he wants featured on his own channel, unlisted if he prefers, and paste the links. That closes C-2 and C-3 in one conversation, gives stable embed URLs, and leaves the permission trail with the person who owns it. Q7 and Q8 exist to get exactly this answer.

Until then P-4 builds against an empty `video_url`: the layout and the create-on-tap behaviour are what P-4 has to prove, and neither needs a real video.

### Honest scope note on the placeholders

Placeholders unblock the build. They do not verify a fact, so **no C task is marked done** and the Must denominator stays 64. P-22 and D-10 are logged as Should. Readiness is unchanged at 19% (12 of 64), Should moves 1 of 7 to 3 of 10.

`PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md` principle 3 says unverified material lives in `/content`, labelled, never in the CMS. This file is that labelled material: a draft of CMS rows, not CMS rows. Entering them is C-11, after the flip-to-live steps.

### Two decisions I did not make for you

1. **P-23**, on how demo rows render in the preview. Rule 8 says unverified content never renders, and `verified` has no third state, so the preview needs an answer. Route A is a filter on the preview environment; route B is a second Framer project holding only demo rows, so the real project starts empty. I lean B and did not pick, because it touches a hard rule and the data model, and both are ask-first items. The rows are paste-ready either way. Full text in demo-dataset sections 8 and 9.
2. The empty-poster treatment borrows the sparkle glyph, which DESIGN section 9 documents only as a bullet or section marker. DESIGN's own rule is that anything not in it needs asking. Approved at P-1, or swap it for the title alone in `--text-muted`.

### Fixes found along the way

- `PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md`'s tree listed no `docs/DESIGN.md`, though the file exists and the same document's file table carried it. Added.
- `content/PLACEHOLDERS.md` registered `[Example Placeholder]` at `content/copy.md` (Hero). Checked: no such bracket exists in that file. Relabelled as an example row with an instruction to delete it before R-4 greps the register, since a phantom entry makes that check look clean when it is not.
- Added the one-source-of-truth pointer from `content/copy.md` SiteSettings to the dataset.
- Roadmap note: two candidate Instagram handles are on file and neither is confirmed, `@alpha.movies_` in the UNVERIFIED research brief and `alpha_movies_ltd`. Neither goes in the footer until Part 2 confirms it.

### Checks run, and what I did not run

Ran: em dash scan on both new files (0); a table column-count validator across all six touched markdown files (all ok); a scorecard recount parsed from the task tables (matches: 12 of 64, Should 3 of 10, R section included, which the previous script skipped); a placeholder token scan (31 unique across 77 fields, every one registered).

Did not run: the unit tests and typecheck. `shared/whatsapp.ts` and `framer/EnquiryForm.tsx` are untouched by this PR, so their 18 tests and strict typecheck from PR #4 still describe this code. The claim that the empty `whatsappDigits` path works as described rests on the jsdom harness from that PR, which did test both number-unset branches, not on anything re-run here.

Nothing was installed. Nothing was deployed. The Framer site is not published.

## Risks

- If route A is chosen for P-23, ESSENTIALS rule 8 gains a documented exception, and future agents will need it spelled out in that file. Say the word and I will write it in the same change.
- The demo dataset is easy to mistake for progress on content. It is progress on the build. The pitch still cannot go out until D-5 is answered, and that is still the critical path.
- `[Owner WhatsApp digits]` is still empty in every path, so the preview will show the copyable brief rather than an Open WhatsApp button until C-8 lands. That is the designed fallback, but it looks different from the intended demo, so it is worth knowing before the walkthrough.

1. **The brief gains three lines PRD section 7 does not show.** `Company:`, `Email:` and
   `Notes:` are appended when filled in. The PRD example does not cover them, but the owner
   cannot serve an agency booking or a diaspora visitor without them, and the PRD itself says
