2. **`buildWhatsAppUrl` refuses a national-format owner number instead of assuming +234.**
   If SiteSettings holds `08012345678`, guessing the country would silently route a diaspora
   owner's enquiries to a stranger's number. It returns `""`, and the confirmation screen then
   shows the copyable brief plus a bracketed email fallback. A lead is never stranded, which is

3. **DESIGN.md section 7 says the confirmation screen should "also show the direct WhatsApp

4. **The component imports only `react`, not `framer`.** So it has no `PropertyControls` and
   Framer will infer the props panel from the prop types. That kept it typecheckable with

   and this file stops typechecking here. Noted in `framer/README.md`.
5. **A 1000 character ceiling on the message.** ARCHITECTURE section 13 item 7 calls it
   "about 1000" and still to be verified, so it is a constant with the notes line absorbing
   the cut. It is dropped whole rather than truncated mid-word if the required lines leave no
   room. Measuring it against a real wa.me link on two phones is a P-18 job.
6. **FR-24's JavaScript-free direct link is not in this component.** A code component cannot
   render without JavaScript, so P-15 has to be a plain Framer text link in the page and the
   footer. The component does render the same link when JS is running.

- `docs/DESIGN.md` section 2 quotes measurements for `assets/brand/alpha-movies-logo-original.png`
  and `assets/brand/alpha-movies-logo.webp`. **Neither the folder nor the files exist in this
  repo**, and `assets/` is not in PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md. Task **F-10**, owner Ademola. I did not
  create the folder and I did not repeat those measurements as fact anywhere.
- PRD section 10 still says `#0A0A0A`; DESIGN section 1 says `#000000` and claims to replace it.
  AGENTS.md only resolves ESSENTIALS-versus-ARCHITECTURE conflicts, not this pair, so I built to
  DESIGN (newer, explicit, sampled from the logo) and opened **F-9** to reconcile the documents
  rather than editing the PRD behind your back.
- DESIGN section 13 refers to **D-9**, **P-21**, **Q11** and **Q12**. None were in ROADMAP.md.
  Added.
- The 13 fields, the option lists and the message format in PRD section 7 are detailed enough to
  build from. That is the first time this repo has had code to check them against, and nothing
  in them turned out to be unbuildable.

## Placeholders introduced (all listed in content/PLACEHOLDERS.md)

`[Starting Price]` (FR-10, PRD Q2), `[Response Time]` (FR-15, PRD Q5), `[Enquiry Email]`
(shown only when the owner number is unset), `[Owner WhatsApp digits]` (PRD Q5, two places by
design), `[Base City]`, `[N]` minimum verified credentials, `[RC number]`, `[Amount]` stats.
Nothing was invented to fill any of them. The form is functional with all of them unset.

The validation and confirmation wording I wrote is registered in `content/copy.md` as the
source of truth and marked for your review. It is not client-supplied copy.

## Honest limits of this PR

- It has never run inside Framer. P-17, P-18 and S-2 are the checks that can still fail it: the
  in-app browser, `target="_blank"`, the real length limit, iOS zoom behaviour, keyboard submit.
- P-14 is `[~]`, not `[x]`. The lines render and hide from props; binding them to the CMS
  SiteSettings needs P-10, which is Framer work.
- P-19 is `[~]`. The register covers the code side; auditing "every demo placeholder is
  bracketed" needs the CMS, which needs P-5 and P-8.
- The short-notice and date-window maths trust the device clock, because Phase 0 has no server.
  ARCHITECTURE 14.2 says never trust it; the Worker computing `short_notice` is the fix, and
  that is behind G1.

## Where the project actually stands after this

Everything left is gated on two things outside a repository: **Emmanuel has never been asked
anything** (D-5 then gate G0, and all of C-1 to C-9 depends on his answers, so the phase guard
blocks C, L, B and R), and **the Framer pages plus the spike need the Framer account** (P-1 to
P-10, P-15 to P-20, S-1 to S-4). I did not mark any of them, and I did not invent content to
make them look done. The next real move is D-5.

No deploy, no Framer publish, no merge. Yours to review.

fix(security): clear the proxy-addr advisory and make a red audit diagnosable from the log
items.body:
## What the gate actually rejected

`.github/workflows/ci.yml:69` runs `npm ci` then `npm audit --audit-level=high`. On `main` at `30fb3ab` that command exits **1**, and `npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high` exits **1** with the same two entries:

| package | resolved (before) | severity | advisory range | direct? | reaches production? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `proxy-addr` | `2.0.7` | **critical** (GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h / CVE-2026-90711, CVSS 9.1) | `1.1.0 - 2.0.7` | no — via `express@5.2.1` | **no, dev-only** |
| `smol-toml` | `1.8.0` | moderate (GHSA-r4xh-jqrq-34v2) | `<= 1.8.0` | no — via `@stellar/stellar-sdk@16.3.1` | yes, production |

`proxy-addr` alone turns the run red: `--audit-level=high` fails on high and critical, and `smol-toml` is moderate, so on its own it would not. Both are cleared here anyway — the bump is semver-compatible and leaving a known-parse-dos in a production dependency to sit at "below threshold" is not a reason to keep it.

```console
$ npm ls proxy-addr
`-- express@5.2.1
  `-- proxy-addr@2.0.8

$ npm ls smol-toml
`-- @stellar/stellar-sdk@16.3.1
  `-- smol-toml@1.9.1
```

## Reconciling the issue's seven entries

The issue says `--package-lock-only` "currently prints 7 entries". At this head both audit modes print **exactly 2** — I could not reproduce the other five, and the issue names only three of them, so this table covers the two reported entries plus the three the issue names. Every "already past range" row was checked against `package-lock.json` at `30fb3ab`, not against the issue text:

| entry | range the issue quotes | lockfile at `30fb3ab` | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `proxy-addr` | `1.1.0 - 2.0.7` | `2.0.7` | **in range** → bumped to `2.0.8` |
| `smol-toml` | `<= 1.8.0` | `1.8.0` | **in range** (moderate, under the gate's threshold) → bumped to `1.9.1` |
| `fastify` | `<= 5.12.4` | `5.12.5` | already resolved past — no action, and not reported by today's audit |
| `@grpc/grpc-js` | `1.14.0 - 1.14.4` | `1.14.5` | already resolved past — same |
| `axios` | `1.0.0 - 1.19.0` | `1.20.0` | already resolved past — same |

The three "already past" packages arrive transitively (`fastify` is a direct dependency at `^5.12.1`, `@grpc/grpc-js` and `axios` come in under the OpenTelemetry and `@x402/*` trees). Bumping them would have been a no-op against ranges they already clear.

## No production dependency was bumped to clear a dev-only advisory

`package.json` is untouched — the whole fix is 12 insertions / 6 deletions in `package-lock.json`. `npm audit fix` was enough because both bumps fall inside ranges that already allow them (`express@5.2.1` wants `^2.0.7`; `@stellar/stellar-sdk@16.3.1` wants `^1.6.1`). I did **not** run `npm audit fix --force`: it wants to move `@stellar/stellar-sdk` `16.3.1` → `17.x`, a breaking major, which the issue explicitly scopes out. If a future advisory only clears on a major, that is its own issue.

## Is a dev-only advisory worth gating CI on? Yes, kept as-is

The issue asks this to be decided explicitly. I kept the installed-tree audit **without** `--omit=dev`. Reason: `express` is a devDependency here, but it is not idle — `examples/http-seller/index.js` and `scripts/e2e.mjs` build a real seller on it, so a spoofing bug in `proxy-addr` is reachable in anything someone runs off this repo. `--omit=dev` would have kept this job green and stopped it ever seeing the class; that is a policy change I am not making as a side effect of a bug fix. Happy to invert it with a written reason if that is the preferred policy.

## Is `src/trust-proxy.js` affected by CVE-2026-90711? No — and now there is a test that says so

The service never calls `proxy-addr`. `resolveClientIp()` in `src/trust-proxy.js` is our own walk: it builds `chain = [peer, ...forwarded.reverse()]` and returns the first entry whose peer is not in the trust list, using `ipMatchesCidr()`. `ipMatchesCidr()` converts an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address to IPv4 before comparing and rejects a prefix wider than the address family has bits — so the CVE's actual failure mode (a trust subnet written `::ffff:10.0.0.0/8` compiling with zero leading bits and matching every IPv4 address, which makes every client look like a trusted proxy) **fails closed here**. That was reasoning about the code, though, and `test/trust-proxy.test.js` had no test for it.

`test/trust-proxy-ipv4-mapped.test.js` pins the behaviour, including the case the fix must not break — a correctly spelled `::ffff:10.0.0.0/104` still matches its own block:

```console
$ node --test test/trust-proxy-ipv4-mapped.test.js
✔ a mapped IPv4 subnet with a short prefix does not believe X-Forwarded-For (5.818584ms)
✔ a zero-leading-bits IPv6 range does not match IPv4 addressees (0.129625ms)
✔ an IPv4-mapped peer still matches a plain IPv4 trust subnet (0.168041ms)
✔ the correctly spelled mapped subnet still matches its own block (0.169667ms)
✔ a mapped X-Forwarded-For entry is not skipped as a trusted hop (0.13225ms)
ℹ tests 5  ℹ pass 5  ℹ fail 0
```

## Making a red run readable from the log

`npm audit --json` reports `vulnerabilities.<name>` as `{name, severity, isDirect, via, effects, range, nodes, fixAvailable}` — **there is no resolved-version field**. The plain-text report prints the advisory range ("proxy-addr 1.1.0 - 2.0.7"), which reads like an accusation against 2.0.7 even when the lockfile already resolves 2.0.8. So the step now prints the resolved version it read from `package-lock.json` at each reported `nodes` path, whether that node is `[dev dependency]` or `[production dependency]`, the advisory range, severity, and whether a fix is available.

The decision command is unchanged: `npm audit --audit-level=high` on the installed tree still gates the job. The diagnostics only run after it fails. The lockfile-only audit is printed for comparison, and the log says in words which of the two CI trusts: the installed tree, because that is what this service ships. Verified against the **pre-fix** lockfile, where it prints:

```
  - node_modules/proxy-addr: resolved 2.0.7 [dev dependency] | advisory range 1.1.0 - 2.0.7 | severity critical | fix available via npm audit fix
  - node_modules/smol-toml: resolved 1.8.0 [production dependency] | advisory range <= 1.8.0 | severity moderate | fix available via npm audit fix
```

## Local verification

All on the committed tree:

| command | result |
|---|---|
| `npm ci` | succeeds against the new lockfile (lockfile is consistent — no drift warning) |
| `npm audit --audit-level=high` | exit **0**, `found 0 vulnerabilities` |
| `npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high` | exit **0** |
| `npm test` | `tests 1409 / pass 1409 / fail 0` (the 5 new tests are discovered by `node --test` and included) |
| `npm run lint` | exit 0 |
| `npm run format:check` | `All matched files use Prettier code style!` |
| `npm run licenses` | exit 0 |
| `npm run env:check` | exit 0 |
| `npm run check:migration` | exit 0 |
| `npm run eval` | exit 0 |

## Two commits, as the issue asks

The issue asks for one commit for the advisory fix and a separate one for the workflow output change:

- `4b5de4b` `fix(deps)` — `package-lock.json` only.
- `565c1d1` `ci(audit)` — the audit step body + `test/trust-proxy-ipv4-mapped.test.js`.

## CI evidence

`ci.yml` ran on this branch: [run 37978023363](https://github.com/accensa/x402-facilitator-stellar/actions/runs/37978023363).

- **`audit` — success**, on the first attempt and again on the re-run. That is the "done" criterion the issue asks for: the gate that was red on `main` at `30fb3ab` is green on this branch.
- `lint`, `format`, `licenses`, `env-doc`, `migration compat`, `eval`, `coverage`, `examples`, `test (node 22)` — all success.
- `test (node 20)` was **red on the first attempt and green on a re-run of the same commit**. That failure is not from this change, and I am not treating the re-run as proof of anything except that the test is timing-sensitive. The evidence is in [the diagnosis comment on this PR](https://github.com/accensa/x402-facilitator-stellar/pull/512#issuecomment-6087678236): the two requests in `test/ip-privacy.test.js` straddled a calendar-minute rate-limit window by 4 ms, which is a pre-existing boundary bug in that test, not an effect of a dev-dependency bump.

## Overlaps with #511 — read before merging either

#511 collapses this workflow into a single `ci` job and therefore rewrites the same region of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Whichever of the two merges second has to carry the other's step body; the merge conflict will be in this exact job, and the `Dependency audit` step name is the thing to keep. If #511 lands first, I will rebase this branch onto main and re-verify both audits before the gate goes green.

#511's single `ci` gate is currently red on its `Dependency audit` step for exactly the advisory this branch clears ([job 113965026666](https://github.com/accensa/x402-facilitator-stellar/actions/runs/37973268647/job/113965026666), step 13 of 13), so this fix is also what makes that PR's gate passable.

Closes #488

items.title: CI: ten jobs -> one required gate, plus the missing pnpm cache
items.body:
## Why

`ci.yml` declared **ten jobs**, each with its own runner lifecycle, its own `npm install -g pnpm@11` and its own **uncached** `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Measured on the last green main run ([run 595](https://github.com/accensa/accensa-app/actions/runs/37315303801), 2026-10-05):

| job | seconds |
|---|---|
| e2e (web) | 157 |
| test (web) | 103 |
| build | 67 |
| typecheck | 56 |
| lint | 55 |
| verify SDK tarball | 46 |
| format | 45 |
| test (sdk) | 39 |
| test (reconcile-payments) | 37 |
| test (prettier config) | 34 |

**639 runner-seconds, ten status-check lines, 160s wall clock.** A PR that breaks prettier formatting turns ten lines red for one mistake.

A PR today gets **11 check lines** (10 from `CI`, 1 from `Visual regression`). After this: **1**.

## What this does

One `ci` job runs the same commands in dependency order after a single install:

`install` → `format:check` → `lint` → root prettier-config `test` → SDK build → SDK test → `gen:api` reproducibility → vector reproducibility → reconcile tests → web tests (`postgres:15` service, job-level now) → `typecheck` → `next build` → `pnpm pack` + ESM/CJS import checks → Playwright browsers → e2e + a11y.

**Nothing was weakened.** Every `run:` is verbatim the command the deleted job ran. No `|| true`, no threshold moved, no retry added, no step deleted from the set of things that are checked. The `Build SDK` step that four separate jobs each repeated now runs once, before the steps that resolve `@accensa/sdk` from `dist`.

Two things that came with the rewrite:

- **`cache: pnpm`.** `pnpm/action-setup@v4` runs *before* `setup-node` (the ordering that action documents for this combination, and the reason a version must be pinned: there is no `packageManager` field in the root `package.json`). This repo has **no dependency cache in CI at all** today, and ten installs is the most expensive thing here that is not a test. The pin is `11.28.5`, which is exactly what `pnpm@11` resolves to on npm right now — so the toolchain is unchanged, it just stops being a moving target.
- **`visual-test.yml` loses its `pull_request` trigger.** Over its 12 runs it went red 10 times and green twice. `playwright.e2e.config.ts` sets `testIgnore: '**/visual.spec.ts'`, so this is the only guard for the committed screenshots — which is why it is demoted to post-merge rather than deleted. It stays runnable with `workflow_dispatch`.

`CONTRIBUTING.md:126` and a comment in `refund-panel.test.tsx` named the old jobs; they now name the steps.

## Ground truth on "required checks"

There is nothing to strip *down to*: `accensa-app/main` has **no branch protection** (`GET /branches/main/protection` → 404), **no rulesets** (`GET /rulesets` → `[]`), and `GET /branches/main` reports `required_status_checks.enforcement_level: "off"`. So **zero required checks** — this PR creates the one candidate gate, it does not make it required. Making it required is repo-settings and your call:

```
gh api -X PUT repos/accensa/accensa-app/branches/main/protection \
  -f required_status_checks[strict]=false \
  -f required_status_checks[contexts][]=ci \
  -f required_pull_request_reviews[required_approving_review_count]=0
```

**Read the next section before running that.**

## The problem this does not fix

Over the 30 most recent `CI` runs, failures per job:

| job | green | red |
|---|---|---|
| format | 16 | 13 |
| test (web) | 21 | 8 |
| build | 22 | 7 |
| typecheck | 22 | 7 |
| e2e (web) | 22 | 6 |
| test (sdk) | 24 | 5 |
| lint | 24 | 5 |
| test (prettier config) | 26 | 3 |
| verify SDK tarball | 26 | 3 |
| test (reconcile-payments) | 26 | 3 |

And across the last 100 runs (2026-09-26 → 2026-10-05): **50 of 70 PR runs red, 17 of 30 main pushes red.**

Consolidation makes that legible — one red line, one named failing step, instead of ten — but it does not repair the underlying breakage. It has a real downside you should price in: **one gate means any of these failures blocks the whole gate**, so requiring `ci` today would reject roughly two of every three merges. Suggested order: merge this, fix the recurring `format` / `test (web)` / `build` reds at root cause, then turn on protection. (For reference: `prettier --check .` is clean at this commit, so this run should not be red for that reason.)

## Deliberately not done here

- **`pnpm --filter @accensa/sdk lint` is an `echo`** — it reports success and checks nothing. Left in place, and flagged in a comment, because fixing it means giving the SDK an ESLint config, which is #511. Deleting the leg silently would narrow what CI checks.
- **No branch protection created**, same as the other repos in this series: repo-settings changes are outside what a PR review can revert.
- `packages/shared` has `lint`/`typecheck` scripts (`tsc --noEmit`) that the root `lint` and `typecheck` scripts do not include. That is an existing gap, untouched here — the root scripts are unchanged.
- Related open issues this interacts with: #527, #530, #528, #512.

## Verification so far

- YAML parses; `jobs` = `[ci]`, 19 steps, service `postgres` (ruby/psych).
- `prettier@3.9.6` (the version the lockfile resolves) `--check` passes on all four edited files and on the whole repo.
- The `ci` workflow runs on this PR; the measured single-job duration goes in a follow-up comment once it finishes.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Chores**
  * Consolidated continuous integration checks into a single workflow, with formatting, linting, package checks, tests, typechecking, and builds run in sequence.
  * Visual tests now run on pushes to `main` that affect the web app or workflow, and can also be started manually. Pull requests targeting `main` no longer trigger them.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated package verification guidance to match the CI check name.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

items.title: ci: one pipeline per pull request
items.body:
## Why

Measured before touching anything:

```
$ gh api repos/accensa/accensa-contracts/branches/main/protection \
    --jq '{has_rsc:(.required_status_checks!=null),approvals:.required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count}'
{"has_rsc":false,"approvals":0}
```

**`main` has no required status checks and requires zero approvals**, so all nine job names a PR shows are advisory — a red pipeline merges anyway. `ci.yml` is the only workflow file, and the last `main` run (**680**, 2026-10-09) cost:

| job | seconds |
|---|---:|
| build-wasm | 543 |
| budget-limits | 229 |
| test | 127 |
| clippy | 28 |
| benchmark-budgets | 26 |
| fmt | 8 |
| changelog & version check | 6 |
| vector parity (cross-repo) | 5 |
| notify accensa-app on vector change | 4 |
| **total** | **976** |

The cost is duplication, not coverage.

## What changed

### One `ci` job, one build

`fmt` → wasm build → `optimize_wasm.sh` → `clippy` → `test` → size budget → Tier A → vector parity → cost-lint → Tier B. Verified duplicates that are gone:

- **Two full workspace wasm builds.** `budget-limits` (`:203`) and `build-wasm` (`:318`) ran the byte-identical `cargo build --locked --workspace --exclude testutils --target wasm32v1-none --release`, each followed by `bash scripts/optimize_wasm.sh`.
- **Two more wasm builds.** `clippy` (`:97`) and `test` (`:126`) each built `-p receipt-shard -p receipt-anchor -p refund-vault` — a subset of the workspace build, so one build feeds all four consumers.
- **The wasm size loop was pasted twice** (`:221-237` and `:335-351`, identical five `package:wasm` pairs).
- **Five cargo cache keys** (`cargo-clippy-`, `cargo-test-`, `cargo-bench-`, `cargo-budget-`, `cargo-wasm-`) warmed five copies of the same `target/`.

### The tolerance the file advertised was never granted

Worth its own paragraph because it changes what you think you are enforcing. The two inline loops compared `SIZE > BUDGET * (1 + WASM_SIZE_TOLERANCE)` with `WASM_SIZE_TOLERANCE: 0.10`, and their comment said "measured value may exceed the committed baseline by up to (1 + tolerance) before the build fails". But `build-wasm` also ran `scripts/check_wasm_budget.sh`, which checks **all 11 contracts** against `.wasm-budget.json` with **no tolerance**, plus the 131,072-byte ledger-entry deploy limit (`:29-31`). The strict one ran on every PR, so the +10% ceiling has never existed in practice: anything the loose loop rejected, the script had already rejected at 100%.

So the loose loops and the now-unused `WASM_SIZE_TOLERANCE` are deleted and the script is the single size gate. Behaviour is unchanged. If you *want* the 10% slack to be real, that is a deliberate change to `check_wasm_budget.sh`, not something to recover from this file.

### `changelog` moves to its own workflow file

It needs no toolchain (6s) and it is the only thing in this repo that reads PR labels (`skip-changelog`). In `ci.yml` its trigger types — `labeled`, `unlabeled` — applied to the whole workflow, so **every label toggle re-ran all 976s**. Now `changelog.yml` keeps all five types for the 6-second job and `ci.yml` drops to `opened, synchronize, reopened`. Same escape hatch, no wasted pipeline.

### Deleted outright

- **`benchmark-budgets`.** Its own comment calls it a "Placeholder for actual budget enforcement" and points at issue 66 - written out without the sigil here so this PR does not read as linked to it; this change is the CI restructure, not that issue's work. It ran `cargo test --locked -p testutils --profile release-with-logs`; `testutils` is a workspace member so its tests still run under `cargo test --locked --workspace`. The only thing lost is that the `release-with-logs` profile is no longer compiled in CI.
- **Both artifact uploads.** `grep -r "download-artifact\|wasm-artifacts\|budget-report-"` across the repo returns nothing outside `ci.yml` itself: `wasm-artifacts-${sha}` and `budget-report-${sha}` had no consumer. They are human-downloadable from the Actions tab, which is the only thing that changes. Issue **#555** (deploy-smoke + fuzz jobs) will build its own wasm rather than decode an artifact — noted there.

### Off the PR path, still on every merge

`if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'` on three steps: the `cargo install --git` of `cargo-budget-report`, the stellar-cli source build that only feeds the script's informational `soroban contract inspect` block, and the Tier B `cargo budget-report --check`.

**The honest cost:** a PR that regresses a Tier B baseline is now caught after merge instead of before. It was already partly true — Tier B needs `STELLAR_TESTNET_SECRET`, so it never ran on fork PRs at all; this makes in-repo PRs behave like fork PRs. If you would rather have the number before merge, restore that one `if:` and accept the install time.

`notify-vector-parity` becomes the step after the parity steps (same ordering guarantee as `needs:`, and `continue-on-error` kept), so it costs PRs no line at all.

### One thing found and deliberately not fixed

`Run soroban-cost-linter` still carries the comment "The step fails only on deny-level (error) findings", and the command ends in:

```
cargo +"$SOROBAN_COST_LINTER_NIGHTLY" cost-lint --workspace --format text | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" || true
```

`|| true` swallows every exit code, and `tee` would mask a pipeline status anyway without `set -o pipefail`. **That step cannot fail**, so the nightly toolchain + dylint + `cargo install` it pays for gates nothing. I kept it as-is: it is the org's own linter being exercised against real contracts (dogfood value, and the findings are in the summary), and deciding whether to un-`|| true` it or drop the install is a separate call from trimming CI. Tell me which and it is a one-line change.

## Ownership respected

- **#556** (`ACCELSA_APP_REF` typo disables the vector-parity pin): the two parity steps are copied **verbatim**, typo included, so that issue's patch still applies.
- **#555**: no artifact dependency introduced; the deleted uploads were unconsumed.

items.title: ci: one status check per pull request
items.body:
## Why

Measured first, because the numbers change the design:

```
$ gh api repos/accensa/x402-facilitator-stellar/branches/main/protection
{"message":"Branch not protected","status":404}
```

**There is no branch protection on `main`, so no check here is required — every one of them is advisory.** A pull request nevertheless shows **12-14 check lines**:

| source | lines per PR |
|---|---|
| `ci.yml` (lint, format, test×2, audit, licenses, env-doc, migration, eval, coverage, examples) | 11 |
| `docs-links.yml` (unfiltered `pull_request`) | 1 |
| `upstream-spec-watch.yml` (paths: `docs/UPSTREAM.md`) | 0-1 |
| `conformance-on-bump.yml` | 0 — see below |

`ci.yml` is the cost centre. Each of its ten jobs does `actions/checkout` + `setup-node` + `npm ci` on the same lockfile. On the last completed `main` run, **420** (2026-10-03):

| job | seconds |
|---|---:|
| coverage | 73 |
| test (node 20) | 66 |
| test (node 22) | 63 |
| examples | 30 |
| format | 19 |
| lint | 19 |
| licenses | 17 |
| eval | 15 |
| audit | 15 |
| env-doc | 14 |
| migration compat | 12 |
| **total** | **343** |

Roughly 220s of that is the commands themselves; the rest is eleven copies of the same setup.

## What changed

### `ci.yml` — ten jobs, one job, all guards kept

A single `ci` job with twelve steps: `npm ci` once, then `lint` → `format:check` → `test` → licence policy → `env:check` → `check:migration` → `eval` → examples install + smoke → `audit`. **Nothing that used to fail a PR now passes one** — every command from the old jobs is present, with its original rationale comment carried down to the step that runs it (#144 for env docs, #190 for the examples smoke test, `docs/MIGRATIONS.md` for the migration rules).

Two ordering decisions:

- **`audit` is last on purpose.** `npm audit --audit-level=high` is about to go red on its own (issue #488: `GHSA-jqcg-44mw-7w3h` in `proxy-addr` via `express@5.2.1`, published 2026-10-05, after the last `main` run). Steps abort on the first failure, so putting an advisory-triggering security gate at the *front* would have hidden whether the tests passed for every contributor. At the end, an advisory red run still shows `Test suite` green in the step list.
- **One Node, 22.** The `['20','22']` matrix is gone. Consequence, stated rather than buried: `package.json` declares `engines: >= 20` and **CI no longer tests that claim at all.** `README.md:161` and `CONTRIBUTING.md:19-21` both asserted the matrix; they now say the range is unverified and point at `nvm use 20 && npm test` if someone wants to prove it. Narrowing `engines` to `>= 22` is the other honest option, and it is its own change.

Trade-off you are accepting: wall-clock. Eleven parallel jobs finished in ~73s; one job runs the same commands in sequence, so a PR waits for the sum. Total runner minutes go down by roughly a third and the `npm ci` count goes from 11 to 1. The measured duration of the consolidated job will be this PR's own `ci` run — I will post it here once it completes rather than estimate it.

### Deleted outright

- **The `coverage` job.** `continue-on-error: true`, no `--fail-under`, no threshold anywhere ("Baseline — no threshold is enforced yet", its own summary footer), not required, and it uploaded `coverage-lcov` with no consumer. It was also the slowest job at 73s. What is lost is the per-directory coverage table in the step summary. Issue #482 asks for coverage data that is *independent and re-runnable*; deleting a non-gating job in CI moves nothing away from that, and arguably helps it.
- **`conformance-on-bump.yml`.** This is the one worth reading twice. It has **zero runs, ever** (`total_count=0` from the API), and the reason is a GitHub footgun: `pull_request.branches` filters the PR's **base** branch, and it was set to `renovate/**`. No pull request is ever opened *against* a renovate branch, so the trigger could not fire — the bump-time conformance gate the docs describe has never existed. It called `conformance-run.yml` directly, which stays (115 runs; `conformance.yml` is its other caller and the schedule that actually fires).

### Off the PR path

- **`docs-links.yml`** now has a path-filtered PR trigger (`docs/**`, its config, itself) instead of an unfiltered one, so code PRs stop paying for a `docs/` link check while doc PRs keep it before merge. `push: main` unchanged.
- **`upstream-spec-watch.yml`** loses its `pull_request` trigger. Two reasons, both about it not being a check: its last step **opens or comments an issue on the base repo** (`issues: write`), which a PR author cannot resolve by fixing their PR; and on a `pull_request` event it reads the baseline SHA and tracked-file list out of **the PR head's copy of `docs/UPSTREAM.md`**, i.e. attacker-chosen text, interpolated into `gh api "repos/…/contents/$f?ref=$BASE"` URLs. The baseline itself is constrained to `[0-9a-f]+`, so this is a scoped-`GITHUB_TOKEN` abuse path rather than a critical one, but removing the trigger removes the input path entirely. Weekly schedule and `workflow_dispatch` are untouched.

### Documentation corrected

The deleted workflow was load-bearing in prose. Three files claimed a bump-time gate that never ran, and one claimed branch protection that does not exist:

- `docs/UPSTREAM.md` — "runs when Renovate opens a PR" and "Branch protection on `main` makes `upstream e2e` a required status check" → replaced with what is true: no bump gate, no branch protection, weekly schedule is the earliest a breaking bump is caught.
- `docs/CONFORMANCE.md` — the same table row ("the PR is blocked on its failure").
- `docs/BAZAAR.md` — "`eval` job" → the `Search evaluation` step of the `ci` job, and "gates merges" qualified, since nothing gates merges here.

## Verification

- All seven remaining workflow files parse (`ruby -ryaml`).
- Every command the single job runs exists: `scripts/check-licenses.mjs`, `check-env-doc.mjs`, `check-migration-compat.js`, `eval/runner.js`, `scripts/smoke-examples.mjs`, plus `examples/{http-seller,mcp-agent}/package-lock.json`.
- `npx prettier@3.9.6 --check` on all eight changed files: **clean** — the new gate would not fail on this PR's own edits.
- `git diff --stat origin/main`: 9 files.

## Open questions for you

1. **Should the `ci` job be *required*?** Right now `main` is unprotected, so this PR reduces noise but enforces nothing. Creating branch protection with `ci` as the required context is a repo-settings change I have deliberately not made — say the word.
2. **`engines: >= 20`** is now unverified. Keep the doc note, restore a second test job for 20, or narrow to `>= 22`?
3. **`external-monitor.yml`** (every 15 minutes, 247 runs) and **`publish-status.yml`** are untouched on purpose: neither is a PR check, and deleting monitoring is a different decision from trimming CI.

Issue #488, #482 and #505 remain open; this PR changes what each is about (and #505's README line is now partly fixed here), not whether they are needed. I will comment on them once this lands so nobody re-derives the measurements above.

* **CI**
  * Consolidated checks into a single CI job on Node 22; checks run sequentially and stop at the first failure.
  * Node 20 is no longer tested in CI, though the package still declares support for Node 20 and later.
  * Coverage reporting has been removed.
  * Pull requests no longer trigger automatic conformance checks for dependency updates; scheduled or manually requested runs remain available.
  * Documentation-link checks now run on pull requests only when relevant files change.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated guidance to clarify CI coverage, search-evaluation reviews, and conformance-check procedures.

items.title: ci: run only the two required checks on pull requests
items.body:
## Why

Branch protection on `main` requires exactly two status contexts, verified with the admin token:

```
$ gh api repos/Tollcraft/soroban-budget-assert/branches/main/protection --jq .required_status_checks.checks
[{"app_id":15368,"context":"budget-check"},{"app_id":15368,"context":"lint"}]
```

A pull request nevertheless shows **six** check lines, because four of them either gate nothing or never run. This PR cuts the PR-time surface down to the two contexts that actually decide a merge, and deletes the rest rather than parking them on another trigger.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| check lines on a PR | 6 | 3 |
| of which real work | 4 | 2 |
| workflows on `pull_request` | 4 files | 2 files |

## What changed

**`coverage.yml` — deleted (74 lines).** The `coverage` job was display-only. `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --exclude amm-pool-contract --exclude host-function-contract --lcov` piped a text summary into `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, then uploaded `lcov.info` as `coverage-report`. There is no threshold step, no `--fail-under`, no artifact consumer, and `coverage` is not a required context — so a dropping percentage could never block a merge. What is lost is the per-PR coverage figure in the step summary; nothing else.

**`release.yml` — tag-only, `publish-dry-run` removed.** This one *did* catch things, and I want the cost on the record rather than in a git blame:

- 91 `pull_request` runs in the last 30 days, **4 failed** (runs `36742445432`, `36428147751`, `36222617893`, `35992684366`).
- Run `36742445432` (2026-09-30, `fix/issues-695-697-698-699`) failed at `Dry run cargo-budget-report` with `error: this file contains an unclosed delimiter` → `error: failed to verify package tarball`. That is genuine publish breakage: without the dry run the same PR reaches `main` and only surfaces when someone tags a release.

So the removal is a real loss of early warning. It is defensible only because the job **was not a required context**, meaning all four of those failures were mergeable anyway — the warning arrived without any gate attached. If you want the signal back, the fix is to re-add this job *and* put `publish-dry-run` in `required_status_checks`, not to leave it non-required. I have kept the measurement in a comment at the top of `release.yml` so the next reader does not re-derive it.

The `if: github.event_name == 'push'` guards on `build`/`checksums`/`publish` are now tautologies. I left them: this PR should not touch the crates.io publish path, and they are behaviourally inert there.

**`deploy-site.yml` — `pull_request` trigger removed** (the `site/**` path filter went with it). `validate` (a link/asset check, `site/scripts/validate.sh`) now runs on the merge to `main` instead of on the PR, so a broken site reference is caught after merge rather than before. `deploy` already gated on `refs/heads/main`, so a site PR was carrying two lines to run one of them.

**`budget.yml` — deliberately untouched.** Both of its jobs stay. `record-history` will still appear as a *skipped* line on PRs, and I did not "fix" that, because the obvious-looking rewrite is wrong:

```yaml
if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'      # today
if: github.event_name == 'push'          # would ALSO fire on `v*` tag pushes
```

`release.yml` is the only other workflow that pushes, and a tag-triggered `record-history` run would call `download-artifact` with `name: budget-report` — an artifact that release runs never publish, so the job would fail on every release. Skipped-not-running is the correct behaviour there. Removing the line entirely means splitting the job into its own push-only workflow file; say the word and I will do it here.

## Deliberately not touched

Two things that looked like dead weight but are not:

- **`quality.yml`'s `cargo-machete` step.** It installs on every PR, which is slow, but it is inside the required `lint` job, so it is part of the gate rather than a check line to strip.
- **`.github/settings.yml:17`**, which requires a context named `Quality Checks` that no workflow has ever emitted. That is the reason [issue #796](https://github.com/Tollcraft/soroban-budget-assert/issues/796) exists. This PR narrows the emitted check set; it does not make that phantom context real, so #796 stays open and I will comment there once this merges so its body does not describe a workflow that no longer runs.

## Verification

- `ruby -ryaml -e "YAML.load_file(f)")` — all four remaining workflow files parse.
- `git diff origin/main --stat`: 3 files, +11 / −96.
- The new check set is visible on this PR itself: the checks tab should list `budget-check`, `lint`, and a skipped `record-history` — and nothing from `Coverage`, `Deploy Site`, or `Release`.

## Merge notes

No secret, permission, or release-behaviour change. Reverting is a `git revert` of one commit; the deleted workflow is recoverable from history.

Closes nothing.

items.title: ci: one status check per pull request
items.body:
## What this changes

A pull request on this repo waited on **8 checks** (and 2 more always-skipped corpus stubs). Branch protection requires exactly **one**: the context `build-and-test`.

After this PR, a PR shows **one check**: `build-and-test`, which is now the job that does the work rather than an aggregator over jobs.

| before | after | why |
|---|---|---|
| `test (ubuntu)` / `test (windows)` / `test (macos)` | `build-and-test` (ubuntu) | same gate commands, one leg |
| `build-and-test` aggregator (`needs:` the above) | the real job | its id is the required context string, so the id is preserved |
| `Coverage Report` | deleted | ran `cargo llvm-cov --test integration` twice over tests `cargo test --workspace` already ran, wrote `lcov.info` to an artifact no workflow downloads (no codecov integration exists), and has no `--fail-under` - it could not fail a build |
| `Performance Benchmark Gate` | deleted | **ran zero benches.** `cargo-cost-lint/Cargo.toml` has no `[[bench]]` target and no `harness = false`, so libtest ignores the custom `fn main()` at `benches/linter_performance.rs:475`; the step logs `0 measured` and exits 0 in ~34s. It fed the only required check. Already tracked as #807 |
| `Validate toolchain pins` in coverage/benchmark | one call | the script was invoked 5x per PR (once per OS leg + both extra jobs) |
| `dogfood-smoke`, `cargo-deny` | PR trigger removed, jobs kept | see below |

## Why the smoke and the advisory scan keep their guarantee

They are not no-signal jobs, so I did not delete them - I took them off the PR path only:

- `dogfood-smoke` still runs on every merge to `main` (and on dispatch), so `action.yml` remains exercised.
- `cargo-deny` still runs on every `main` push that touches `**/Cargo.lock`, `**/Cargo.toml` or `deny.toml`, and daily at 06:00 UTC.
- The nightly `discover-corpus` / `dogfood-corpus` matrix (the false-positive regression baseline against `tests/corpus/baseline.json`) is untouched; it was never a PR check.

## The cost, stated plainly

- A PR that breaks Windows or macOS path handling now fails only after merge. The deleted legs were `cargo test --workspace` on those runners; the suite itself is unchanged.
- A dependency advisory introduced by a PR is first detected on merge or at the next 06:00 UTC run, not on the PR.
- Coverage numbers stop being reported at all (nothing consumed them).
- `build-and-test` is a single point of failure for merges - which is what "one required check" means.

## Deliberately kept intact

`shared-key: cost-linter` and `cache-directories: tests/corpus/.shared-target` on the rust-cache step. `Swatinem/rust-cache` embeds the job name in its default key; the file's own comment says renaming the job discards every cache entry. The new job reuses the id the matrix leg's cache was keyed to, so PRs keep restoring a warm `target/` instead of rebuilding dylint and the workspace cold.

The corpus-baseline bootstrap (`if grep -q '"contracts": {}' tests/corpus/baseline.json`) is preserved verbatim; it is what lets a first run bless the baseline instead of failing.

## Verification run

- Parsed all six workflow files (ruby/psych): valid, and exactly one job has a `pull_request` trigger - `lint.yml / build-and-test`. `container-publish`, `nightly-bump`, `publish` never trigger on PRs, before or after.
- Confirmed the required context string against live protection: `gh api repos/Tollcraft/soroban-cost-linter/branches/main/protection/required_status_checks` returns `build-and-test`, `strict=false`. The new job has that **id** and no `name:` key, so it reports that exact context. If either changes later, the repo stops being mergeable.
- Confirmed the benchmark claim before deleting: `git show origin/main:cargo-cost-lint/Cargo.toml | grep -A3 '\[\[bench\]\]'` - no match.
- This branch's own CI run is the remaining proof: it should show one check, named `build-and-test`, marked required.

## Relationship to open issues

- **#807** (benchmark gate records zero measured operations): this PR deletes the gate instead of repairing it, which resolves the symptom but not the underlying missing `[[bench]]` target. If you want the benchmark itself kept, that issue is the place; I did not touch `benches/linter_performance.rs`.
- No other open issue claims `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, `dogfood-action.yml` or `security.yml` as its file region, and this PR changes nothing outside those three files.

items.title: docs(roadmap): open Post-MVP Accuracy & Coverage with six pre-filed boxes
items.body:
## What this changes

One file, added lines only: `ROADMAP.md` gains a `## Post-MVP Accuracy & Coverage` section at the end of the document, with **six unchecked boxes — one per issue, #252 through #257** — and a short lead paragraph explaining why the section exists before the work does.

No code, no dependency, no CI change, no test change. No existing line of the roadmap is edited, reordered, or re-ticked; the only edit outside the new section is the blank line that keeps the heading separated from the paragraph above it, matching every other `## ` in this file.

## Why

The six post-ladder issues filed today (#252–#257) each end with the same instruction from the org template: tick this work's box in `ROADMAP.md`. None of those boxes exists yet.

Left as they are, every one of the six contributors writes to the same position — the end of the same file, under a heading each one invents slightly differently. Six PRs whose diffs collide on a section that carries **no technical dependency at all**, so merge conflicts and rebases get spent on a formatting collision instead of on the work. That is a coordination cost paid six times to buy nothing.

Pre-partitioning the surface removes it: the section is landed once, here, and each contributing PR ticks exactly its own line and touches nothing else in this file. Six separate regions of the diff, no shared lines.

The box wording names the **result** each issue must produce, not the plan it uses. Several of these issues ask the contributor to measure something before choosing an approach — a box that pre-committed to the approach would read like a decision already made.

Two ownership decisions are recorded in the box text, because they are what makes the set parallel-safe and a contributor reads this file before they read their issue:

- **#254 is the sole owner of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`** among the open issues. It wires `build-and-test` to consume `build-fixture`'s uploaded artifact so the two `#[ignore]`d real-contract cases gate every pull request, and it is the only PR in the set that edits that workflow.
- **#256 gets a new `.github/workflows/docs.yml`** (`RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps`) rather than a job added to `ci.yml`. That deletes the one genuine collision between the CI issue and the rustdoc issue: after this split the two do not meet in a file at all.

## How it was verified

Box arithmetic, counted rather than remembered — `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*- \[(x| )\]' ROADMAP.md`:

```
origin/main                                    111 checked, 0 unchecked
this branch                                    111 checked,  6 unchecked
```

The 6 is exactly the six new lines; no previously-checked box moved to unchecked. Confirmed against `git show origin/main:ROADMAP.md` in this same worktree.

Nothing under `src/` or `tests/` reads this file as data — the only occurrence in code is a prose mention of a box's wording in `src/source_map/mod.rs:68` — so six unchecked boxes break no gate. `Tollcraft/docs` publishes the roadmap's counts on its own page, and that page is re-synced to `111 checked / 6 unchecked` alongside this PR.

Gates, run in this worktree at `94f994b` + this commit:

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean, no output.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — `Finished dev profile … in 6.53s`, zero warnings.
- `cargo test --workspace` — **255 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored** across 9 test binaries. The two ignored tests are the pre-existing real-contract cases, `the_real_soroban_contract_build_runs_and_its_host_calls_are_costed` (`tests/cli_e2e.rs:1146`) and `the_real_soroban_build_resolves_contract_lines` (`tests/source_map_fixture.rs:262`) — #254's subject, untouched here.

No user-visible behavior changes: this PR adds no flag, no output, and no binary path, so the built-binary check below is not applicable rather than skipped.

## Roadmap

- [x] `ROADMAP.md` is updated by this branch — the update *is* the contribution. The PR does not tick a box for itself, and adding one would be self-referential bookkeeping: the six boxes it creates are the record, and each is ticked by the PR that does the work. #257 is the one issue in the set permitted to edit boxes outside this new section, to dedupe the two identical `#163` lines in Phase 3.

## Scope

- [x] Only what the coordination problem asked for: the new section, its lead paragraph, and the blank line before the heading. No rename, reformat, or "while I was here" edit anywhere else in the file or the repo.
- [x] Issues #252–#257 are named **without** closing keywords — this branch finishes none of them, and a `Closes` on any of them would close an issue nobody has implemented yet.
- [x] MVP constraints still hold (`AGENTS.md`, `ARCHITECTURE_ESSENTIALS.md`): no tracing macros in the user's contract, no `inferno`/SVG dependency, no hand-written `gimli` parser, no per-instruction heap. Nothing here touches any of them.
- [ ] Both CI jobs (`Build and Test`, `Build Fixture`) green and the branch current with `main`; a red gate is fixed at its cause, never loosened.

Part of the post-ladder wave opened 2026-10-08, after the Phase 5/6 ladder closed at 0 open issues.

---

No `Closes #` line: this branch finishes none of #252–#257, and the template warns that automation here reads more references as closings than GitHub does.

items.body:
## What this changes

Documentation only — two files, +29/−8 lines, no code, no dependency, no CI change.

| File | What changes |
| :--- | :--- |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | One bullet in "Keeping the contributor grid current" (the section #249 added) is rewritten so the check it documents is an **equality** rather than a quoted figure. The per-author-name counts (`adajala` 32, `Ademola` 22, `WAGMI` 17) go away; the names stay. |
| `ROADMAP.md` | The `Documentation Upkeep` entry's matching sentence is rewritten the same way, and a new checked box records this fix. |

Nothing else in the section moves: the `gh api` + `--jq` command, the "do not add a tile by hand / do not
re-sort" rule, the `web-flow` exclusion, the GitHub-served avatars and the `per_page=100` note are unchanged.
`README.md` is not touched.

## Why

Issue #250, and it is a defect this branch's own parent created. #249 proved that the contributors endpoint
groups by GitHub *account* with a number — "`wagmiiii` appears once at 71 … `git log --format='%ae' origin/main |
grep -cE 'ademola2993k@gmail.com|130152505'` prints 71". The equality was measured and real; the problem is that
the merge which carried that sentence (`d30a28f`, this repository's own squash merge) added a new commit under
those same two addresses. So the section became false roughly two minutes after it became true: a contributor
following its instructions today runs the grep, gets **72**, and finds the documented cross-check disagreeing
with the documented prose — in the one file whose whole argument is that every claim here can be checked by
running something. That is precisely the "claim with no command behind it" failure the section exists to prevent,
arriving from the other direction: a command behind a claim that no longer matches it.

**What is left:** nothing. The invariant is now what the section asks the reader to verify, and the dated figures
stay as dated measurements.

## How it was verified

**The disagreement itself, measured on the merged `main`:**

| account | endpoint `contributions` | `git log --format='%ae' origin/main \| grep -cE …` |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| `wagmiiii` (two addresses) | 71 | **72** |
| `mallison031` | 19 | 19 |
| `Gabbydunkk` (two addresses) | 6 | 6 |

The only account whose count moved is the one whose commit `d30a28f` just added, and it moved on the git side
first — re-polled minutes later the endpoint still reports 71. So the text says the endpoint *trails* the newest
commit rather than disagreeing with the history, which is what a grid that prints its own date is built to
absorb. The claim is written as the equality plus a measurement stamped 2026-10-08, so the next merge moves both
sides and the sentence stays true.

**The check that was *not* broken, re-run anyway** — because this branch edits the file that documents it:

```
$ awk '/^## Keeping the contributor grid current/,/^Four choices/' CONTRIBUTING.md \
    | sed -n '/^```sh$/,/^```$/p' | sed '1d;$d' | sh   # via GH_TOKEN, exit 0
15
$ diff <(that output) <(sed -n '640,654p' README.md) && echo "BYTE-IDENTICAL"
BYTE-IDENTICAL
```

The documented command was again extracted from `CONTRIBUTING.md` itself rather than retyped, and it still
reproduces `README.md`'s fifteen tile lines byte for byte against the post-merge tree — so #249's central claim
survives, and this diff does not quietly invalidate it.

Gates, run twice from `.worktrees/grid-drift` (once before the final wording edit, once on the committed tree

items.title: test(bench): measure the profiler against the same run without it (#188)
items.body:
## What this answers

Issue 188 asks for the profiler's end-to-end overhead against raw execution, "reported as a concrete multiplier". Before this branch the only number the repository could produce was `record_step` at ~2.4 ns — the cheapest function in the crate, timed on its own, with no denominator next to it. This diff adds that denominator and the stages between it and a profiling run.

**The headline: a profiled run costs 1.16–1.21× the same contract run with the profiler switched off — and the tracer is not what that multiplier pays for.**

## How `benches/tracer_benchmark.rs` is now laid out

One invocation of the committed `fixtures/dwarf_probe/dwarf_probe.wasm`, export `caller_of_heavy`, timed at five stages. Each stage adds exactly one thing to the previous one, so the total decomposes instead of being asserted:

| bench | what it adds |
|---|---|
| `execution/raw` | `Engine::default()`, no fuel, no hook, direct `Func::call` — **the denominator** |
| `execution/metered_no_hook` | `setup_engine()` + `set_fuel(u64::MAX)` — this profiler's engine *configuration*, tracing off |
| `execution/traced_sample_1000` | `invoke_function` installs the call hook; events taken with `flush_trace` the way `run_target` takes them |
| `execution/traced_sample_1` | same, at `--sample-rate 1` |
| `pipeline/profile_and_format` | + `ProfileAggregator::aggregate` + `OutputFormatter::to_collapsed_stack` |

`setup(metered, sample_rate)` builds store and instance the way `run_target` does — engine, module, state, fuel, instantiation, and the results buffer sized and typed off the export's signature — so `execution/raw` and `pipeline/profile_and_format` differ only in the profiler, not in how the call is reached. `record_step` is kept as its own bench.

No new dependency (criterion 0.8 was already declared for these two `[[bench]]` targets), `std::hint::black_box` rather than the deprecated `criterion::black_box`, and no gate touched — `cargo bench` is not CI, and this PR does not make it one.

## The numbers

Medians of three 100-sample passes, Apple M1 Pro, rustc 1.98.1, Darwin 27.0.0:

| bench | pass 1 | pass 2 | pass 3 | × raw |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `execution/raw` | 3.796 µs | 3.922 µs | 3.861 µs | 1.00 |
| `execution/metered_no_hook` | 4.410 | 4.348 | 4.370 | **1.11–1.16** |
| `execution/traced_sample_1000` | 4.457 | 4.357 | 4.280 | 1.11–1.17 |
| `execution/traced_sample_1` | 4.475 | 4.410 | 4.405 | 1.12–1.18 |
| `pipeline/profile_and_format` | 4.608 | 4.686 | 4.481 | **1.16–1.21** |
| `record_step` | 2.434 ns | 2.379 ns | 2.414 ns | — |

The decomposition, which is the part a reader should actually check:

- **Fuel metering is the overhead**: 1.11–1.16× all by itself, before any tracing exists.
- **The call hook adds nothing measurable on top of metering**: 0.98–1.02×, i.e. inside this suite's own pass-to-pass spread (`execution/raw` itself varies ~3%). That is what a boundary-only hook predicts — this fixture crosses **two** boundaries per invocation, confirmed from the binary: `--sample-rate 1` writes `wasm[0] 2` where the default writes `wasm[0] 0`. Two `record_step` calls at ~2.4 ns are ~5 ns of a 4,400 ns run.
- **`--sample-rate` has no cost to save today.** The two rates are within ≤3% of each other, which is the suite's noise floor. The flag is only a lever once there is an instruction hook for it to throttle, which is #213's territory; `src/tracer.rs:352-356` documents the boundary-only substitution and this is its measurement.
- **Aggregation + collapsed-stack formatting**: 1.02–1.08× over the metered baseline.

## The same split from the CLI

The issue asks for wall-clock, so this is the built binary (`cargo build --release` on this branch), n=30 per point, three repeats, medians:

| command | median |
|---|---|
| `--version` (process floor) | 2.74–2.84 ms |
| `--wasm … --fn <unknown>` (read + translate module, then exit 1) | 2.80–2.93 ms |
| full profile run (writes `.folded`) | 3.51–3.55 ms |
| same at `--sample-rate 1` | 3.48–3.52 ms |

So a user pays ≈**1.25–1.3× the process floor per invocation**, of which reading and translating the module is 0.04–0.09 ms and instantiate + run + profile + write is 0.61–0.71 ms — against a timed in-process pipeline stage of ~4.5 µs. End-to-end, the overhead is not execution either; and `--sample-rate 1` again moves nothing (−0.04 to 0.00 ms).

## Deliberate scope calls, stated

- The issue's task line named "raw `cargo test` execution" as the comparator. This uses the same call through the same `Store` with the profiler switched off instead, because a debug-profile test harness times allocator, harness startup and `#[test]` plumbing alongside execution and cannot support a multiplier claim *about the profiler*. `execution/raw` is the same code path minus the profiler, which is the comparison the number is claiming.
- The figures live in `ROADMAP.md` and this body, not in a `docs/` page: a benchmark quoted in prose with no command behind it silently rots, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` now says claims have to come with the command that produced them. `docs/internals/` is untouched.
- Nothing here changes a cost, a flag, or a limitation. The `.folded` output is unchanged; `cargo test --workspace` is 182 tests + 5 doc-tests green with 2 `#[ignore]`d, `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass on this branch.

Closes #188

items.body:
## What this changes

`CONTRIBUTING.md`, from 20 lines to 152. Issue 187 asks for a file "covering workflow guidelines" whose done-state is "document covers **setup and PR expectations**". The file had the Roadmap Rule and a section called "Code Quality Standards" whose entire content was *"run the appropriate formatters, linters, and tests for this repository"* — it named no command, listed no PR expectation beyond "include the roadmap update", and said nothing about setup at all. So this PR fills in the two halves the issue names, and **every command in it was run on this branch** rather than copied from a template.

## Setup

* Toolchain floor stated as Rust 1.85+ because the crate is edition 2024 — `Cargo.toml` carries no `rust-version`, so the edition is the evidence and the README's existing claim is the source.
* `cargo build`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo run -- --help` — the last run here; it prints the two-mode summary.
* The two things a first-time contributor actually trips on, both from reading the repo rather than guessing:
  * The root `Cargo.toml` is a **workspace** (`members = [".", "fixtures/dummy-contract"]`) and pins `ed25519-dalek` to `vendor/ed25519-dalek-2.1.1` through `[patch.crates-io]`. That pin is what keeps `soroban-env-host`'s testutils resolvable against a `rand_core` they compile, per the comment above it, so it is described as load-bearing rather than incidental.
  * **Where the wasm fixture lands.** `./fixtures/build.sh` is runnable from anywhere (it `cd`s to its own directory — verified), and because the contract is a workspace member its artifact goes to **the repository root's `target/`**: measured at `target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/dummy_contract.wasm`, 622,522 B, which is the path `REAL_BUILD` reads in `tests/cli_e2e.rs:35-38`. It is *not* under `fixtures/dummy-contract/target/`, which is where a standalone crate would put it — the surprise is the part worth writing down, so the file says both halves.
* The two cases that need it are named — `the_real_soroban_contract_build_still_stops_at_its_host_imports` and `the_real_soroban_build_resolves_contract_lines` — with `cargo test -- --ignored` as how to run them, **measured green on this branch**. Before the fixture build they fail loudly with `… — run fixtures/build.sh` instead of passing quietly, and the file says why that is the repo's rule (a check that silently skips is worse than one plainly outside the default run) and what makes the first of them sharper: it asserts a **limitation**, so the PR that removes that limitation must invert it — written in the test, not in a comment.

## The gates CI runs

A table of exactly what `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs, plus the two facts a contributor learns from a red job:

* `Build and Test` = `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`. `--all-targets` covers `tests/` and `benches/`, so an unused `mut` in a test you just added is enough to fail; `-D warnings` makes any lint a failure.
* Doc-tests run inside `cargo test --workspace` (5 here), which is why a `///` example that drifts from the API fails in CI rather than in review.
* `Build Fixture` compiles the wasm with the `wasm32` target — nothing else guards a fixture that stops building.
* `cargo bench` is named as the two criterion benches and explicitly marked **not** a gate, so a reader does not treat a benchmark as a required check.

## PR expectations

Written as the conventions this repository's merged PRs already follow, so they are learnable before the first review rather than from one: assignment before starting; branch from current `main`, one issue per branch; `ROADMAP.md` checked **in the same branch**, with what makes an entry useful (a code change names its test, a docs change names the command that produced the output it quotes); a breakdown body per rule 6 of `AGENTS.md`; **exactly one** closing line, with other issues named without a closing keyword because a `Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves` on an issue your diff does not finish closes somebody else's open work; claims backed by a command actually run, and a citation to the line when the claim is about code (`src/tracer.rs:352-356` is used as the example, since that is what the last five docs PRs cited); behavior tested through the built binary as a process rather than an in-process `Result`; scope kept to the issue.

The four MVP constraints are gathered where a contributor meets them **before designing** — zero instrumentation, no `inferno`/SVG renderer, no hand-written DWARF parsing, no mass allocation per traced step — with the reason each exists rather than just the prohibition.

Merge expectations are stated as what happens here today: both jobs green, branch current, a red gate fixed at its cause and never loosened, no `--no-verify`, squash-merge with the issue number in the subject so the history reads as one commit per closed box.

## Out of scope

Documentation only: one file rewritten, one `ROADMAP.md` Phase 5 box checked. No code, no flag, no dependency, no CI change, no issue-label taxonomy. The on-ramp points at the two labels that exist in this repo (`good first issue`, `help wanted`, checked against the label list) and at `PRD.md`'s edge-case section rather than at a hand-curated starter list this file would then have to keep current.

## Gates

* `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
* `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
* `cargo test --workspace` — green, doc-tests included.
* `cargo test -- --ignored` after `./fixtures/build.sh` — both fixture cases green (that pair is also the evidence for the setup section above).

The branch carries a merge of current `main` so `ROADMAP.md` keeps both Phase 5 entries in order rather than overwriting the tutorial one.

Closes #187

items.title: docs(tutorial): a contract, a profile, a flamegraph, start to finish
items.body:
## What this adds

`docs/tutorial.md` — the eight-step end-to-end path issue 178 asks for: build the profiler, compile a contract that keeps its line tables, profile one export, understand the `.folded` file, open it in Speedscope, see what a real `soroban-sdk` build does, diff two runs, and know where to go next. Plus one pointer line in README's Getting Started and one README correction described below.

**Every transcript in the file is measured**, off a `cargo build --release` binary built from this branch's base (`ac8fd36`), over a contract the reader compiles themselves from the source in step 2. No invented output, no plausible-looking stack.

## The three claims that prose could have faked, checked against the machine

**(a) The `debug` precondition, exercised rather than cited.** README has told readers to keep line tables since issue 175 and nobody had followed that instruction end to end. This fixture adds `[profile.profiling] inherits = "release"; debug = "line-tables-only"` to a three-function `#![no_std]` cdylib: the profiling build is **1,482 B against release's 714 B**, carrying `.debug_info`, `.debug_line`, `.debug_abbrev`, `.debug_ranges`, `.debug_str` and a `name` section. rustc's `-C debuginfo=1` really does emit `.debug_info`, so `SourceMapper::new` is satisfiable from this recipe and the profiler stays silent about the build. The same paragraph states the honest opposite of what a reader hopes — line tables do not make *today's* picture rich, because the tracer is handed no program counter to look a line up with — which is what keeps step 2 separate from issue 210's follow-ups.

**(b) The zero, shown as a zero.** Step 3 is the real first run: `no function recorded any exclusive cost (cpu)` on stdout, `wasm[0] 0` in the file, and no warning on stderr — that silence is itself the check that the build recipe worked, so the tutorial contrasts it with the same contract built by plain `cargo build --release`, which prints the name-section-without-line-tables warning verbatim and still exits `0`. Then the structural explanation: two boundaries per invocation (`src/tracer.rs:352-356`), an accumulator that gains 1 per boundary never crossing the default `--sample-rate 1000`. And `--sample-rate 1` measured to `wasm[0] 2` so the tracer is visibly alive.

**(c) The viewer claim, verified in a browser.** speedscope.app was actually driven with the file this tutorial produces: it logs `Importing as collapsed stack format` and switches to the Time Order / Left Heavy / Sandwich view, so the steps say drag-onto-the-window or **Browse**, which is what the app offers, and note that nothing leaves the browser. The chart is **one bar**, presented as the honest picture of a single-frame trace and the shape PC attribution fills in (`wasm[0];total;sum_squares` named as the future path). `flamegraph.pl` is offered as an optional external reader only — this repository bundles no SVG renderer and promises none (AGENTS.md).

## The wall is step 6, not a footnote

Point the same command at this repository's own `soroban-sdk` fixture (what `fixtures/build.sh` leaves in `fixtures/dummy-contract/target/…/release/`, ~622 KB) and the reader meets two measured refusals in their own order:

- `--fn call` → `error: 'call' is not an exported function; the module exports _, compute_heavy_loop, memory_heavy_loop`, exit `1`.
- `--fn compute_heavy_loop --output dummy.folded` → `error: failed to instantiate module: cannot find definition for import (i,_) with type Func(FuncType { core: FuncType { params: [I64], results: [I64] } })`, exit `1`, **and no file on disk** — checked against both the named output and the default `profile.folded`, because nothing ran.

That is issue 210 stated as the single blocker between this tutorial and a version that profiles the reader's actual contract, with issue 211 (exports that take arguments) and issue 212 (ledger state) named as neighbours — and the reason steps 2 and 3 use an SDK-free contract, said out loud rather than left for a reader to infer.

## Step 7's diff is a measured pair

`wasm[0] 0 2 +2` / `total 0 2 +2` / `1 of 1 functions changed cost, 0 unchanged`, from the two runs in step 3. It carries a trap the tutorial now names: the last row is `total`, which `src/formatter.rs:370-371` builds as the **whole-profile sum**, not a function — so in a tutorial whose export is also named `total`, the row that looks like the entry point is the tally underneath it. Also stated: a regression still exits `0`, and a `.folded` records no metric of its own, so both sides of a `compare` must have agreed on `--metric` beforehand and nothing can check it.

## One README line corrected by measurement

README's Getting Started told readers to open the file in speedscope via `File → Open`. The app does not offer that; it offers a drop zone and a **Browse** button, which is what the verified session used. The same block now points at `docs/tutorial.md` too.

## Deliberately out of scope

Documentation only: one new file, one pointer, that one correction. No code, no flag, no dependency, no new fixture in git (the tutorial's contract is source the reader pastes, and the Soroban artifact it quotes is the fixture `fixtures/build.sh` already builds). No `inferno`/SVG renderer, no instrumentation of user code, no per-instruction allocation — the ceilings in AGENTS.md are unchanged by this diff.

## Gates

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo test --workspace` — all suites green, doc-tests included, the one pre-existing `#[ignore]` (the 622 KB fixture artifact, not in git) unchanged.

Closes #178

items.body:
Closes #137

## Summary
Composite contract health score (0–100) computed by the indexer each poll, persisted, served via `GET /api/v1/contracts/{id}/health-score`, and surfaced on the contract detail page.

## Weights
| Component | Weight |
|---|---|
| Uptime | 40% |
| Error rate | 25% |
| Performance | 20% |
| Storage TTL | 15% |

- Uptime: healthy/total watchdog checks (fallback to watchdog status).
- Error rate: 100·(successful/total) over the window.
- Performance: ratio of recent per-invocation cost vs baseline; ratio 1→100, 1.5x→50, ≥2x→0.
- Storage TTL: share of storage entries with headroom beyond the health horizon.

Overall = weighted sum /100, clamped 0–100.

## Changes
- **API**: migration `000007_contract_health_scores`, `HealthScoreStore` (postgres + mock), handler `GET /api/v1/contracts/{id}/health-score` with router + scopes.
- **Indexer**: pure `healthscore` package (Compute + weights) with unit tests; poller `runHealthScores` job writes each cycle; interfaces/store mirrored.
- **Web**: `HealthScoreResponse` type + `getContractHealthScore`, self-fetching `HealthScoreCard` on the contract detail page.

## Verification
- `apps/api`: build, vet, tests green.
- `services/indexer`: build, vet, tests green.
- `apps/web`: only pre-existing HEAD errors remain (AlertSubscription-family, unrelated).

items.title: feat: track contract Wasm-hash upgrades across indexer and API (#129)
items.body:
Closes #129

## Summary

Detects when a tracked contract's on-chain Wasm code changes (contract upgrade) and records it as a `contract_upgrades` row, coupled to the existing tracked contract list.

## Changes

**services/indexer**
- New `internal/wasm` package: `ContractInstanceKey` builds the XDR LedgerKey for a contract's instance entry; `WasmHashFromInstanceEntry` decodes the 32-byte Wasm hash from an instance `ContractData` entry (best-effort, `ok=false` on mismatch).
- `poller.go`: `checkWasmHash` runs after the poll lock and before event scanning:
  - first observation (no stored hash) → baselines the stored hash.
  - hash differs from stored → inserts a `ContractUpgrade` row (`FromHash`/`ToHash`/`Ledger`/`At`) and updates the stored hash.
  - errors are logged and non-fatal; one contract's upgrade lookup can't block the poll pass.
- `interfaces.go`: added `GetLedgerEntries`, `InsertContractUpgrade`, `UpdateContractWasmHash` to `RPCClient`/`Store`.
- `main.go` stubs cover the new interface methods.
- Tests: baseline, upgrade-on-change (verifies from/to/ledger), and no-change cases via a fake RPC/store.

**apps/api**
- Migration `000006_contract_upgrades` + `contract_upgrades` store queries.

items.title: feat(watchdog): implement batch contract registration
items.body:
## Summary
Adds `register_contracts_batch` to the watchdog contract so projects with many contracts can register them all in a single transaction instead of one call per contract. This cuts transaction fees and network round-trips for protocols monitoring many contracts.

Closes #100

## Changes
- New `Registration` (`{ contract_id, name, check_interval }`) and `BatchResult` (`Success` / `Skipped(String)`) contract types.
- `register_contracts_batch(env, caller, registrations) -> Vec<BatchResult>`:
  - Applies each entry independently; a duplicate or zero check-interval is skipped without reverting the whole batch.
  - Emits `ContractRegistered` for every successful registration.
  - Enforces a max batch size of 20 before processing anything.
  - Returns empty results for an empty batch (no panic).
  - Auth matches `register_contract` (caller `require_auth` + admin/owner gate).
- Refactors the single `register_contract` to share the storage/event logic via a `store_registration` helper so the two paths can't drift.

## Verification
- `cargo test` in `contracts/watchdog`: 16 tests pass, including the 5 new ones (happy path, duplicate skip, max exceeded, invalid interval skip, empty batch).
- `cargo fmt --check` clean.

Key files:
- `contracts/watchdog/src/lib.rs`
